Various categories are available, as well as options for young participants and a virtual race.

name: Modine Söderköpings Stadslopp
organizer: Norrköpings Löparklubb i samarbete med Söderköpings OK

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Alla barn deltar som vanligt helt gratis i Ramunderstaden Lilla Brunnsparksloppet.

description: Modine Söderköping City Run is a fast, popular 5-kilometre race starting and finishing in Brunnsparken in Söderköping. The seventh edition takes place on Tuesday, 16 June 2026, on a flat, easy-to-run course suited to both fast runners and recreational participants. The course is lined with music stations and a large cheering crowd. After finishing, participants are treated to a summer platter from ICA Supermarket. The event also includes the free Ramunderstaden Little Brunnsparken Run for children, with several age groups.
course_highlights: Flat, fast 5 km course (officially measured by federation measurer Per Lindh)
Start and finish in Brunnsparken, Söderköping
Music stations and strong crowd support along the course
additional: Race bib collection: ICA Supermarket Söderköping, Monday 15 June, 12:00–18:00; remaining bibs can be collected in the start/finish area up to one hour before the start. The timing chip is attached as a tab at the top of the bib and must not be removed. Water is available at the start/finish and at 2.8 km. World Class leads the warm-up (15 minutes before each start; the children’s races warm up at 16:45). After finishing, ICA Supermarket serves a summer platter; massage is available after the race. Late registration: online and on site. Online registration is open through 14 June at 16:00, according to the information provided. The regular late-registration period (increased fee of 50 SEK, for a total of 375 SEK) runs from 8 June until one hour before the start; late registration is also available on site/at bib collection (the website’s news page lists the on-site fee as 345 SEK). The 5 km course runs through Söderköping; the start/finish area is in Brunnsparken; chip timing by Racetimer; warm-up before the start led by World Class; water at the start/finish and at 2.8 km; a medal for all participants; bag/outerwear drop-off at the start and finish; the Little Brunnsparken Run (1.1 km) for children; registration via the website; bibs collected at ICA Söderköping.

name: Blodomloppet (Visby)
description: Welcome to Blodomloppet in Visby—a community running event that raises awareness of blood donation. You can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km, or take part in Lilla Blodomloppet. The courses pass through Visby’s cultural heritage areas and are open to both recreational runners and teams. The event is organised locally by VIF Gute Friidrott together with the blood donation centre in Visby, and often ends with a picnic and activities for participants.
course_highlights: The 5 km and 10 km courses run along Visby’s ring wall and through the town centre
The 10 km course includes the seafront promenade, Almedalen and Visby harbour
Scenic historic surroundings close to the town
additional: Team registration is available and costs 1,750 kr up to and including 26 May; groups can register many participants using an Excel template imported during registration; the event highlights blood donation and provides information about gifts for blood donors; local organisers: VIF Gute Friidrott (contact: Annie Gardell, Tel 0733 909722, email visby@blodomloppet.se) and the Blood Donation Centre in Visby (Tel 0498-26 84 53, email blodcentralen@gotland.se). There are three categories: 10 km, 5 km and Lilla Blodomloppet; registration via blodomloppet.se; start times in Visby are listed on the website; included: technical T-shirt, race bib and medal; team registration is available for companies and groups; the event is streamed live on blodomloppet.se.

name: Filter Temposari (3. etapp)
location: Vabaduse väljak, Tallinn, Harju County, Estonia
description: Filter Temposari is Estonia’s oldest and most prestigious time-trial series, offering the chance to test yourself in cycling, running or roller skating. The series takes place at various locations in Tallinn and its surroundings, featuring speed races with staggered starts. The Tallinn event takes place at Freedom Square, where the course is short and technical, making it well suited to sprint enthusiasts. The series’ finishers can take part in the Kullapada prize programme, which rewards consistent participation in every stage.
course_highlights: Staggered-start cycling races on a speed course around Tallinn
Short 1.3 km sprints in the heart of Tallinn at Freedom Square
Roller skating on roads with good surfaces
additional: The event has a fast group, whose riders are invited by name for the final 10 minutes. Warming up on the course during the competition is prohibited, but free warm-up rollers are available at the event centre. Participants must obey traffic laws, as most of the course is not closed to cars. The Kullapada prize programme rewards everyone who finishes all stages of the season. The event features varied terrain and offers registration and several distance options, including courses of 1.3 km and up to 5 km.

name: Kohila pikamaajooksude sari 2026 IV etapp 400m
location: Kohila Spordikeskuse staadion, Kohila, Rapla County, Estonia

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Stardimaks 8 eurot, kuni 19a ja pensionärid 5 eurot

description: The Kohila Distance Running Series 2026, Stage IV, is a 400 m event held at the Kohila Sports Centre stadium and is open to everyone interested in running. The series offers various distances and age groups, with participants earning points according to their placing in each race. The entry fee is €8, or €5 for young people and pensioners, payable in cash on site. Pre-registration is recommended and closes at 16:30 on race day; those registering later will be placed in the later races. Series winners are determined by age group, and the awards ceremony takes place at the end of the series.
course_highlights: A 400 m race around the stadium
Races take place on the tartan track at the Kohila Sports Centre stadium
The series includes various age groups and distances from 400 m to 5,000 m
additional: Pre-registration closes at 16:30 on race day; those registering later will be placed in the later races. On-site registration closes at 18:30. Races start with the fastest heats. The top 10 finishers in each race earn points, and the best six races count toward the series standings. The awards ceremony takes place after the final event; participants must compete in at least four stages to qualify for a prize. The entry fee is payable in cash on site; pre-registration is available on the website; events take place at Kohila Stadium; age groups and points system.

name: Kohila Pikamaajooksusari
description: The Kohila Long-Distance Running Series is a sports series organised by Kohila Parish, consisting of several stages and aimed at sports enthusiasts in the area. Its goal is to promote sport and physical activity and give participants the opportunity to compete over various distances. Participants receive a commemorative medal at each stage, and points are awarded in competition classes across the series. The series is organised by Kohila Sports Centre, which supports a healthy lifestyle and active movement.
course_highlights: Multi-stage long-distance running series in Kohila Parish
Points awarded throughout the series and a commemorative medal for every stage finisher
Suitable for runners of different ability levels
additional: The series includes several stages over various distances, such as 800m, 2000m and 5000m. All participants receive a commemorative medal at every stage. Health checks are recommended before the competitions. Events are held mostly in the evenings, for example at 19:00. The series also includes 800-metre races, and participants can collect points throughout the season. The event is open to all age groups and offers opportunities to be active in a supportive community atmosphere.

name: KEVEK ja Tartu Kalev staadionijooksu sari
description: The KEVEK and Tartu Kalev Stadium Running Series is a track-and-field series organized by Tartu Kalev Sports Society, offering the opportunity to take part in several meets at stadiums in Tartu and Ülenurme. The series aims to provide competition opportunities for children and young people and promote participation in athletics in the city and county of Tartu. Meets take place during the summer months and are open to different age groups. Registration closes at 12:00 on race day, allowing for flexible participation.
course_highlights: Meets take place at Tartu Tamme and Ülenurme stadiums
The series includes several meets over the summer, including the June 6 and July 8 meets
Suitable for children and young people interested in athletics
additional: The 6th and 7th meets will take place at Ülenurme Stadium due to track resurfacing. Registration closes at 12:00 on race day. Madsa Sports and Recreation Centre is a supporter and offers a sports base in Valga County, 11 km from Otepää. The meets will take place on June 17, 2026, at Tartu Kalev Stadium. Registration is open, and participants can receive results and take part in various distances.

name: Midsommarjoggen 2026
description: Midsommarjoggen is a running festival in Rynningeviken Nature Reserve in Örebro, taking place on 17 June 2026. The main race is 7.2 km, mostly on easy-to-run gravel paths along the water and through the forest. It suits both runners looking to run fast and those who prefer to jog or walk at a summer pace. The course passes Rävgången and Naturens Hus and finishes with an after-run gathering at Stora Hjortstorps gård, with food, drinks and good company. There is also a KidsRun (approximately 600 m) for children born in 2016 or later.
course_highlights: 7.2 km, mostly easy-to-run gravel paths along the water in Rynningeviken
Passes Rävgången and Naturens Hus, with evening sunshine and lake views
Two wooden bridges over Lillån and two longer hills by Venastugan
additional: Start at 18:30 (warm-up at 18:15; compulsory race briefing at 18:25). KidsRun starts at 17:45 (gather at 17:40). Bib numbers can be collected from the race office from 16:00; collect by 18:10 at the latest. Timing uses a loaned transponder (800 kr charged for a lost transponder); KidsRun is not timed. Water/energy stations at 3 and 5 km; toilets are available in the event area and at the water stations. No changing facilities or showers on site. After-run gathering at Stora Hjortstorps gård (BBQ 299 SEK, including water and coffee; half price for children under 12). Youth (born in 2008 or later) receive a 50% discount; group registration via info@epictrail.se. The course is described as 7.2 km in Rynningeviken Nature Reserve. Transponders are loaned at the start and must be returned (800 kr charged if lost). Food and drinks are provided along the course, followed by an after-run gathering at Stora Hjortstorps Gård (BBQ buffet 299 SEK, including water and coffee). No changing rooms or showers. Kids Run is not timed. The entry fee includes a place in the race, bib number, timing, medal, sports drink and energy.

name: Rakvere lahtised MV
description: The Rakvere Open Championships are an athletics competition held at Rakvere Stadium. The event brings together the local sports community and offers the chance to watch competitions in a variety of athletics events. It is open to everyone and creates a sporty, supportive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The competitions take place at Rakvere Stadium
A variety of athletics events
A local sports community and supportive atmosphere
additional: The competitions are open to all participants, and registration takes place on site. The entry fee is 5 euros for participants living outside Lääne-Viru County.

name: Tallinna noorte MV
description: The Tallinn Youth Championships are an individual athletics competition for young people and adults, held in Tallinn. The competition includes several age groups, from U-14 to adults, and various athletics events such as running, jumping, shot put and throwing. Its aim is to honour the memory of Eerik Konist and promote athletics among young people. Medal awards are given in all age groups, and special prizes go to the top performers. The competition takes place at a stadium and starts at 11:00 in the morning; registration opens at 10:00.
course_highlights: A varied athletics programme: running, jumping, shot put and throwing
The competition takes place at Heino Lipp Stadium
Competitors are allowed 4 attempts in jumping, shot put and throwing events
additional: Registration opens at 10:00, and technical entries must be submitted half an hour before the competition begins. The top three in each event and age group are awarded medals, with additional special prizes for the best boys and girls. The chief judge is Viktor Predbannikov and the head secretary is Lilia Schmidt (tel. 5069887). The competition includes various events such as sprinting, long-distance running, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus and javelin. Participants can experience competition and the joy of sport at a regional level.

name: Tänndalen 100 miles
location: Tännäs, Härjedalen Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden

name: Borejoggen

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lagjoggen följer samma priser som Borejoggen, alltså 300:-/person och ytterligare 50:- per person vid efteranmälan.

description: Borejoggen is a traditional Midsummer race in Torsby, welcoming elite runners, recreational runners and children. The main race is run on asphalt through central Torsby and is approximately 8.5 km. Minijoggen is a shorter class of approximately 1.5 km for children and young people. There is also Lagjoggen, a team race for teams of three, with the team’s combined time counting. The start is in the area around Östmarksvägen/Herrgårdsparken (Minijoggen at 09:30; Borejoggen and Lagjoggen at 11:00). Registration is via RaceID or at Prima Sport/Herrgårdsparken, according to the organiser’s information.
course_highlights: The main course is approximately 8.5 km on asphalt through central Torsby
Minijoggen is approximately 1.5 km for children and young people
Water stations at 2 km, 5.8 km and the finish
additional: The start is on Östmarksvägen/Herrgårdsparken. Race numbers and timing chips can be collected at Prima Sport during Midsummer week. Changing facilities and showers are available at Björnevi IP and Valbergsstugan; toilets are available at Herrgårdsparken and Björnevi IP. Prizes are offered, including sprint and hill prizes and prize money for the winners. Traffic marshals will be stationed on busy roads, and medical services will be available at the finish. The course is 8.5 km on asphalt through central Torsby. Start times are 9:30 for Minijoggen and 11:00 for Borejoggen/Lagjoggen. Registration is via RaceID or Prima Sport. Lagjoggen requires three participants per team. Water stations are provided as specified for the course.

name: Orsakajtn
description: Orsakajt'n and Orsabajk'n are an MTB and running race held every year on Midsummer Eve in Orsa. The event offers a unique combination of cycling and running in beautiful natural surroundings and attracts both young people and adults. Race numbers are sent digitally in advance, and bibs can be picked up at Karl Hedin in Orsa or at the start venue. A licence and membership in an association affiliated with the Swedish Cycling Federation are required for the MTB competition categories.
course_highlights: MTB and running race in scenic Orsa
Always held on Midsummer Eve
A licence and membership in a cycling federation are required for the MTB competition categories
additional: Registration opens on 29 April 2026. The entry fee increases by 50% from 16 June. No on-site entries; registration closes one hour before the start. Race numbers are sent digitally on 17 June. Bibs can be picked up on 18 June from 16:00 to 20:00 at Karl Hedin in Orsa or at the start venue on race day. No refunds for injury or illness. A licence is required for the MTB categories. Registration is online, and race numbers are available on mobile. Held in scenic Orsa.

name: Kuusalu valla kergej. MV
description: The Kuusalu Municipality Athletics Championships is a traditional athletics competition held in Kuusalu. Participants compete in various age groups and distances, offering opportunities for both recreational and more experienced athletes. The event is dedicated to the memory of Margus Keerma and is organized by the Treeningpartner sports club. The competition is a great opportunity to showcase your skills and enjoy a sporting atmosphere in Kuusalu Municipality.
course_highlights: A variety of athletics events
Competition for different age groups
A community sporting event
additional: The competition takes place at Kuusalu Stadium and includes various athletics events. Registration takes place before the competition begins.

name: Ümber Saadjärve jooks

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lastejooksudel osalemine on eelregistreerimisel kuni 18.06 TASUTA

description: The 38th Around Lake Saadjärv Run takes place on 20 June 2026 in Kukulinna, offering participants a 17 km run and a fitness walk around Lake Saadjärv. The course follows a paved road and has three drink stations to support runners during the event. In addition to the main run, the programme includes children’s races in different age groups and a fitness walk suitable for everyone who enjoys being active. Every finisher receives a commemorative medal, and the best participants are awarded prizes by age group. This traditional, well-organised event offers an enjoyable sporting experience for the whole family.
course_highlights: 17 km run around Lake Saadjärv on a paved road
Three drink stations at kilometres 5, 9 and 14
Start and finish by the Ice Age Centre
additional: The main run entry fee includes a race bib, timing service, course support, a drink at the finish, awards for the best participants and a participant medal. The fitness walk also has timing and a medal. On race day, payment is possible only in cash. Transfers to another participant are free until 17.06.2026 and cost 5 euros on race day. The shorter children’s race distances are not timed; the 9–10-year-old race is timed. The timing service partner is OÜ Teamtime, and results will be published at teamtime.ee/results. Registration is open until 18 June 2026. Participants are offered a medal, with awards in different age groups. The entry fee ranges from 15 to 20 EUR, and the children’s races are free. The course includes paved roads and trails and is equipped with drink stations.

name: Pasvalio maratonas
location: Pasvalio kultūros ir poilsio parko stadionas, Pasvalys, Pasvalio rajonas, Lietuva
organizer: Bėgimo mėgėjų ir sveikos gyvensenos klubas „Vėtra“, Lietuvos bėgimo mėgėjų asociacija, Pasvalio sporto mokykla
description: The Pasvalys Marathon is a traditional running event held in the city of Pasvalys. It aims to promote running among young people and adults and encourage a healthy lifestyle. The event takes place at the stadium in Pasvalys Culture and Recreation Park, where participants compete in the marathon, half-marathon, and children’s race. The course length and number of laps are adjusted for the different distances, with water and refreshment stations every 5 km. Participants receive prizes and commemorative medals, and the event is part of the Pasvalys City Festival “Vys par to ãlo” programme.
course_highlights: 10 km course; 4 laps for the marathon and 2 laps for the half-marathon
Water and refreshment stations every 5 km
Start and finish at the stadium in Pasvalys Culture and Recreation Park
additional: Race numbers are distributed from 8:00 at Pasvalys Stadium. The children’s 400 m race starts at 11:00. Participants must have a doctor’s permission or an application bearing a doctor’s approval; otherwise, they are responsible for their own health during the competition. Participants who finish within the time limit receive commemorative medals. Various distances are offered, and participants can look forward to medals, certificates, prizes, and refreshments.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 4. Pariisi Maastikujooks
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 brings together health-conscious runners and recreational athletes from spring to autumn, offering a variety of running and walking options. The series aims to promote healthy lifestyles and encourage local people to take part in sporting events. The 4th Pariisi Trail Run takes place on 21 June at Pariisi Holiday Village and is part of a long-running series featuring different age groups and distance options. Timing is chip-based, and race numbers must be attached to the abdomen or chest, reflecting the organisers’ attention to participants’ comfort and safety.
course_highlights: Trail run at Pariisi Holiday Village
Distances from 5 km to 10 km for the main races
Various age groups and race categories
additional: Timing is provided by a chip attached to the back of the race number and covered with a foam pad. Race numbers must be attached to the abdomen or chest, not the back. Pre-registration closes at 16:00 on the day before the race. On-site registration takes place at the times specified in the race guide. The series also includes walking distances from 1.8 km to 10 km. The event offers various distances, including up to 10 km, 5 km, 1.6 km, and short courses for young participants and children. Participants can register online, and the event supports healthy lifestyles and community sports.

name: Mapri Ehitus x Vägilase jooks Rummu
description: Mapri Ehitus x Vägilase jooks Rummu is a varied obstacle race held at the Rummu quarry. On the course, participants climb, crawl, lift and haul their way through mud, water, sand and hills, making it a challenge for everyone. The race is part of the Vägilase jooks series, known as Estonia’s best OCR event. The course is more substantial and offers exciting obstacles and experiences in nature.
course_highlights: 4 km and 8 km distances
Mud, water, sand and hills
Varied obstacles and technical challenges
additional: Register for at least three Vägilase jooks events at once to receive a 15% season discount. Participants under 20 and seniors aged 60 and over receive an automatic 30% discount based on their year of birth. A 20% group discount applies when at least 4 people register for the same event. Children’s races are free when registered online in advance; registration on site costs €3. The children’s races feature manageable obstacles and medals for all finishers. Starts take place in waves, with groups of 8 starting every 2 minutes. Participants may make unlimited attempts at obstacles; failing to complete an obstacle means losing their wristband. Obstacle race, children’s races, registration online and via Stebby, season discounts and invoices, competition categories and start groups, safety and alternative exercises at obstacles

name: Maraton igas linnas Keila
description: Marathon in Every City Keila is a unique running event that gives participants the opportunity to run a marathon distance in different cities. There are refreshment stations along the course every 400 metres, as well as toilets, making the run comfortable and supporting athletes’ wellbeing. The event is suitable both for experienced marathon runners and for those who want to test their endurance. It is well organised and offers a pleasant experience for all participants.
course_highlights: The marathon course runs through city streets and a stadium
Refreshment stations every 400 metres
The risk of getting lost on the course is minimal thanks to clear markings
additional: The marathon takes place at a stadium and on city streets, with a refreshment station and toilet every 400 metres. The risk of getting lost on the course is eliminated thanks to clear markings. The event takes place in the city of Iisaku, offering the chance to enjoy a stadium-based course and take part in different running distances.

name: Midsommartrail - Möt ljuset
description: Midsommartrail – Meet the Light is a personal trail race held on the longest day of the year, with the experience at its heart. The race starts before dawn so you can run into the daylight along a 30 km route through beautiful forest terrain. The number of participants is limited (maximum 100) to create an intimate and considerate atmosphere, and after the finish the organizers serve a generous breakfast. Navigation is by a GPS route provided in advance and a map at the start, and there are two aid stations along the way.
course_highlights: 30 km of trail running at dawn, meeting the light along the route
Two aid stations along the route
Navigation using a GPS route and map (runners are responsible for their own navigation)
additional: Start/finish at Attunda Orienteering Club’s clubhouse, Ytterbyvägen 22, Sollentuna; easiest public transport: commuter train to Rotebro (1.5 km walk); parking at Sollentuna Golf Club (500 m walk); parking on Ytterbyvägen is not permitted; maximum 100 participants; breakfast served after the race; registration open until one hour before the start; minimum age 18. Recommended accommodation: Good Morning Hotel Sollentuna (discount code NIGHTTRAILRUN). Start time: 02:00 on 2026-06-21. 30 km trail run; GPS route and map; two aid stations along the way; breakfast after the finish; hotel discount at Good Morning Hotel Sollentuna with code NIGHTTRAILRUN.

name: Night Trail Run  Sommar 2025
description: Night Trail Run Sommartrail is a personal trail race in Sollentuna, held on the longest day of the year. The race is 30 km long and starts at dawn, giving participants the experience of meeting the summer light. Participant numbers are limited to preserve an intimate atmosphere. Participants navigate using a GPS route, sent in advance, and are also given a map at the start. After the finish, a hearty breakfast is served so you can share the experience with the other runners.
course_highlights: 30 km of trail running, starting before dawn and reaching daylight
Participants navigate themselves using a GPS route and a map provided at the start
Two energy stations along the course and breakfast after the finish
additional: Maximum 100 runners. Start/finish at Attunda Orienteering Clubhouse, Ytterbyvägen 22 in Sollentuna. Nearest public transport: commuter train to Rotebro station, followed by an approximately 1.5 km walk to the venue. Parking is recommended at Sollentuna Golf Club (approximately 500 m away); parking on Ytterbyvägen is not permitted. Participants are responsible for navigating; the GPS route is sent in advance and a map is handed out at the start. Registration is open until one hour before the race starts. Minimum age: 18. Recommended accommodation: Good Morning Hotel Sollentuna (discount code NIGHTTRAILRUN). Seasonal versions include Sommartrail, Hösttrail and Hundtrail, with the experience and the nighttime experience highlighted as the essence of Night Trail Run.

name: Pärnumaa Võidupüha maraton
description: The Pärnumaa Victory Day Marathon takes place on 22 June 2026 in Tori Parish, with the event centre located beside the historic Tori Estonian Soldiers’ Memorial Church. The marathon brings several new features and is organised in cooperation with the Pärnumaa Sports Association and supporters. It is a traditional and legendary race, offering athletes a varied and memorable experience.
course_highlights: Event centre beside the legendary Tori Estonian Soldiers’ Memorial Church
Varied and historic course through the Pärnumaa landscape
Organised in cooperation with the Pärnumaa Sports Association and Tori Parish
additional: The event centre for all distances is located beside the legendary and historic Tori Estonian Soldiers’ Memorial Church. The event is organised by Tori Parish in cooperation with the Pärnumaa Sports Association and supporters. Volunteers will be involved in the event. The marathon will use a new course, and the event is part of the Victory Day celebrations in Pärnumaa.

name: Häädemeeste Võidupüha jooks
description: The Häädemeeste Victory Day Run is a traditional running event held near the Häädemeeste bus station. The event invites everyone who enjoys being active to celebrate Victory Day in a sporting and community-minded spirit. In addition to the main race, a children’s run for the youngest members of the family will be held for the first time. After the run, participants can enjoy the Midsummer celebration at Häädemeeste Summer Garden. Participation is free, and registration takes place on site.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Häädemeeste bus station
Children’s run before the main race
Midsummer celebration at Häädemeeste Summer Garden after the run
additional: Registration and gathering take place on site at the Häädemeeste bus station from 16:00 to 17:30. Participation is free.

name: 49. Jaanijooks ümber Karksi-Nuia paisjärve
location: Karksi ordulinnuse varemed, Karksi-Nuia, Põhja-Sakala vald, Estonia
description: The 49th Jaanijooks around the Karksi-Nuia reservoir is a traditional running race held near the ruins of Karksi Order Castle. The race follows a route around the picturesque Karksi-Nuia reservoir, offering participants beautiful views and an enjoyable running experience. The event is intended for both recreational and experienced runners, and offers a chance to enjoy an active day in the community.
course_highlights: A run around the Karksi-Nuia reservoir
Picturesque views of the reservoir and the castle ruins
Rural and forest roads, suitable for different types of runners
additional: The event is part of the local community’s sports calendar and takes place near a historic site, giving participants the chance to experience nature and history at the same time.

name: Jooks suvesse
description: The Pööripäevajooksud are an annual race series consisting of several stages, where participants can earn points and compete in age groups. Jooks suvesse is one of the series’ stages and takes place in Loode tammik in Kuressaare. The course has varied terrain, including a shared-use path and forest roads, which may be muddy depending on the weather. Participants are provided with electronic timing, reusable race bibs and drinking cups, and a sweet treat and drink at the finish.
course_highlights: The loop is 2,346 metres long
About 600 metres of the course is on a shared-use path
Three quarters of the course runs through the forest on dirt/gravel roads
additional: Reusable race bibs with timing chips, which must be returned after the race. The entry fee is paid in cash on site. There is a small car park at the finish, as well as parking along the roadside. All competitors receive a diploma at the finish, and prizes are awarded to the three fastest in each age group. Taking part in at least three stages qualifies participants to receive a diploma and trophy for the season overall. The event includes various running activities and gives participants the chance to enjoy the summer atmosphere of Saaremaa.

name: Jaanijooks ümber Karksi-Nuia paisjärve
description: Jaanijooks around the Karksi-Nuia reservoir is a traditional road race held in the Karksi-Nuia area. The race gives participants the chance to enjoy the beautiful surroundings of the lake and take on a sporting challenge. The event is organized by MTÜ Karksi Sport, which is dedicated to promoting local sports. Jaanijooks is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to take part in a friendly and supportive environment.
course_highlights: A run around the Karksi-Nuia reservoir
Beautiful lakeside scenery
Road surfaces and pedestrian and cycle paths
additional: Participants can register online or on race day. Participants have the opportunity to receive awards and use a race bib and chip. Health and insurance liability for participants is also addressed as part of the event.

name: 12. Rõuge maastikujooks-kõnd
description: The 12th Rõuge Trail Run and Walk is a trail running and Nordic walking event held in the beautiful Rõuge Ööbikuorg, Võru County, offering participants the chance to enjoy nature and exercise. The event is suitable for runners, Nordic walkers and walkers looking to spend time actively. The Centre of Excellence for Physical Activity organizes the event to promote physical activity and a healthy lifestyle. Participants can experience beautiful scenery and the joy of movement while supporting their well-being.
course_highlights: Beautiful scenery in Rõuge Ööbikuorg
Suitable for running, Nordic walking and walking
A nature-rich route in Võru County
additional: The route includes forest trails and hiking trails; the event promotes physical activity and health; registration and further information are unavailable.

name: Böda Beach Run
location: Böda Sand-stranden, Löttorp, Borgholm Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Böda Beach Run is a race that stands out at Böda Sand. It is a challenging competition on sand and in water, suited both to those looking to compete and to families looking to have fun, with courses ranging from 500 metres to 10 km. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. The event is held at Böda Sand Beach Resort on 24 June.
course_highlights: Courses from 500 m to 10 km
A challenging competition on sand and in water
A medal for everyone who finishes
additional: Date: 24 June. The event takes place at Böda Sand Beach Resort (Bödasandsallén 11, 387 73 Löttorp). Contact/phone for Böda Sand: (+46)485-22200. The event is promoted as family-friendly and recurring in the resort’s events calendar. Special accommodation offers are available at Böda Sand; late registration and race-number pickup take place at Nordpoolen at 12:00 on race day.

name: Karlstad Stadslopp
description: Karlstad Stadslopp is a popular 10 km race in Karlstad, with something for every runner—from those chasing a personal best to those who want to enjoy the community atmosphere along the Klarälven. The event offers the classic 10 km, a shorter 5 km, and the Karlstad Minilopp and Miniminilopp for younger participants. The race starts at Tingvallabron and finishes in Museiparken; the 2026 edition opens SM‑veckan and will be broadcast on SVT. The organiser, IF Göta Karlstad, welcomes participants of all ages and experience levels.
course_highlights: Start at Tingvallabron
Finish in Museiparken
Route along the Klarälven
additional: When registering, provide an estimated finish time for seeding; young people born in 2008 or later and students receive a 100 kr discount during certain periods; a 10 km team competition is available (at least six participants per team)—contact tavling@ifgota.se to register a team; payment via PlusGiro (47 37 91-2), with instructions for the race category and name; gift vouchers can be purchased via PG and notified to info@ifgota.se; participant information (PM) is sent by email and published on the website; After Run and a concert in Museiparken are part of the opening of SM‑veckan; the race is part of SM‑veckan 2026 and will be broadcast on SVT. The race offers 10 km and 5 km, as well as the Karlstad Minilopp (ages 7–12) and Miniminilopp (ages 0–6). Minimum age: 12; dogs are not allowed; walkers with a stroller or rollator may start in the last start group; participation is at your own risk; entry fees are non-refundable; publication of photos on the website and social media is permitted.

name: Trosa Stadslopp
description: Trosa Stadslopp is a long-running community celebration, always held on the first Friday after Midsummer. In 2026, the race takes place on Friday, 26 June. The course runs through picturesque summer-time Trosa, with large crowds and close to the water, creating a summery atmosphere for both competition and recreation. The event offers categories for elite runners, recreational runners, young people and children, as well as the 8,900 m main race and shorter recreational options.
course_highlights: The course runs through picturesque summer-time Trosa, close to the water
The 8,900 m main race, plus the 4 km Jogging/Walking with poles event and a 700 m children's race
Start and finish at Trosa square, with large crowds and stage activities
additional: Registration remains open until the start, and payment can be made by Swish or card; alternatively, pay to Trosa Stadslopp's bankgiro 488-8335. Folksam recreational race insurance is available (e.g. SEK 155 for basic cover, Startklar Plus SEK 275). Bib collection opens at 10:00 at Team Sportia on race day. The 8,900 m main race has start groups based on target times (start group 1 at 21:00, followed by additional groups); there is also a children's race (700 m) and award ceremonies on stage. The organiser gives 50 cl of Vitamin Well to runners in the 8,900 m and 4 km races. The programme also includes 700 m and 900 m distances, Jogging/Walking with poles over 4 km, and information about night buses to Stockholm after the race.

name: Sillamäe promenaadijooks

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lastejooks (450 m) / Tillujooks (150 m) - TASUTA; Noortejooks (3,5 km) ajavõtuta TASUTA; Noortejooks (3,5 km) ajavõtuga TASUTA

description: Sillamäe Promenade Run is a well-known city race held near the Sillamäe Cultural Centre. The race tradition began as a stair run, and since 2021 it has been called the Promenade Run. The event offers various distances, from short runs for little ones to the adults’ 7 km main distance, which also challenges trained athletes. It is a community-focused and engaging event, with several activities in addition to running, and an important contribution from supporters and volunteers.
course_highlights: The 7 km main distance includes the Sillamäe stairs—the race’s toughest but most beautiful climb
Shorter distances for children and young people: 150 m, 450 m and 3.5 km
A city run along the Sillamäe promenade and stairs
additional: Registration takes place online and usually closes one month before the race. The participation fee must be paid to the account of the Sillamäe School Sports Association. The event also features volunteers, several supporters, and additional activities such as dancing, singing, cycling and basketball shooting. The race is organised by several local sports organisations and schools. The event includes various distance options and cultural activities and is aimed at engaging the community. Participants can also enjoy beautiful nature and views of the sea.

name: EUTR - Estonia Ultra-Trail Race
description: The 9th edition of the Estonia Ultra-Trail Race (EUTR) will take place on 26–27 June 2026 in Narva, Ida-Virumaa, Estonia. The race starts and finishes at the Akkekula (Nut Hill) sports complex. Organized by the non-commercial sports club SK ETR, the event features trails certified by the International Trail Running Association (ITRA), with ITRA points awarded to finishers. The race offers several distances for trail runners of different levels, including an ultra-trail and shorter trail options.
course_highlights: 126 km Ultra-Trail distance with 4 ITRA qualification points
63 km Trail distance with 2 ITRA qualification points
33 km Trail distance with 1 ITRA qualification point
additional: Reregistration is possible for a fee of 15 EUR, plus any price difference when changing distance. The race offers changing rooms, storage facilities, and an EXPO area. Registration for the Breakout® race for athletes with disabilities using wheelchairs is closed. The organizer reserves the right to use photos and videos taken during the event indefinitely. The event offers various distances, including ultramarathon, trail, and wheelchair racing. Registration and schedule information are available on the website.

name: Jordgubbslunken
description: Jordgubbslunken is a popular rural race in Rudskoga with the motto “walk, jog, run.” The event offers Lilla Lunken (6 km) and Stora Lunken (10 km), as well as Minilunken for children (born in 2017 or later). The start and finish are at Grunnebacka School, and the courses follow Rudskoga’s winding village roads through a beautiful cultural landscape. At the finish, all participants receive one litre of strawberries. There are also many prizes, plus a grand prize drawn using participants’ race numbers.
course_highlights: 6 km loop on gravel
10 km loop alternating between gravel roads and closely mown grass
Start and finish at Grunnebacka School; courses follow winding village roads through a cultural landscape
additional: Always held on the first Saturday after Midsummer; categories for men, women and children; Minilunken for children born in 2017 or later; all participants receive one litre of strawberries at the finish; many prizes, with a grand prize drawn using participants’ race numbers; information about this year’s race is published under “På gång i Rudskoga” on the website. The 6 km loop is on gravel, while the 10 km loop alternates between gravel roads and closely mown grass. Start at 15:00. On-site registration by 14:30 (a higher fee applies for on-site registration). Payment via Bankgiro 505-1404 or Swish 1233296605; questions can be directed to the listed phone numbers.

name: Silverleden Ultra 100 Miles
description: Silverleden Ultra is a trail ultramarathon in Bergslagen, held in Hällefors with the start and finish at Hurtigtorpet over the weekend of 26–27 June 2026. The event offers distances of 33 km, 64 km and 100 miles and is promoted with slogans such as “Running joy”, “Both long & gruesome” and “Run. Survive. Brag” — a technical, hilly event for those seeking a tough experience in nature. The 100-mile class is full for 2026. The race is aimed at experienced ultrarunners and runners looking to challenge themselves on rocky, root-covered and hilly terrain.
course_highlights: Technical trails with many hills; most of the longer climbs are in the second half of the course
Roots and rock slabs that become very slippery in wet weather — trail shoes with deep lugs are recommended
Aid station at Silvergruvan (approximately 35 km) — option to have poles transported to the aid station
additional: Bus: transport from Hurtigtorpet to the 33 km start departs at 10:30. Places are limited and must be booked in advance (by 2026-06-20). Accommodation: several local options are listed within 5–20 km of the start/finish. A limited number of caravan and motorhome pitches are available — please contact info@silverledenultra.se. Electricity is available in limited supply but cannot be guaranteed. There is no facility for charging electric cars at the start/finish at Hurtigtorpet. The minimum participant age is 15 (the year they turn 15); relay teams cannot be entered in 2026. International participants can pay using the IBAN provided; the order confirmation from the registration system can be used to claim a wellness allowance. Early Bird prices are mentioned in the information, but exact amounts are not given.

name: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi
location: Ottsjö, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi is a non-competitive mountain event where participants can choose between two point-to-point routes (approximately 24 km or 42 km) and enjoy both mountain scenery and local food. The routes are marked, and food stations (approximately every 7 km) serve local ingredients prepared and served in the mountains in collaboration with local producers. New routes have been created for 2026: the longer route starts and finishes in Ottsjö, while the shorter route starts in Trillevallen and finishes in Ottsjö. The event has an open start time so participants can enjoy the experience at their own pace, but early starts are recommended for those planning to walk slowly.
course_highlights: Point-to-point routes through mountain terrain, with 24 km and 42 km options
Food stations approximately every 7 km, serving local dishes in the mountains
2026 routes: the longer route starts and finishes in Ottsjö; the shorter route starts in Trillevallen and finishes in Ottsjö
additional: Non-competitive format with an open start; an early start is recommended for slower walkers. Transfers to the start are available and can be booked (transfer bookings open approximately two weeks before the event). The organizer recommends staying at Trillevallens Högfjällshotell or in Ottsjö (contact details are available on the page). Event information memos contain transport and logistics details. Open start times allow for a relaxed pace; food stations approximately every 7 km feature local producers; accommodation suggestions include Trillevallens Högfjällshotell or Ottsjö; bus transfers to the start are available from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker; electronic timing and transport logistics are managed by the event.

name: Silverleden Ultra
description: Silverleden Ultra is a trail race in Hällefors/Bergslagen, with distances of 64 km, 33 km and 100 miles. The race takes place on 26 - 27 June 2026 and is promoted under the slogan “the joy of running” — participants can expect technical, hilly terrain with plenty of trails and climbs. The 100-mile race is sold out for 2026. The organiser’s copy and information emphasise challenging routes close to nature, and recommend bringing the right equipment.
course_highlights: Hilly terrain with many climbs — the bigger climbs are mainly in the second half of the course
Technical trails with roots and rock slabs; trail shoes with a deep tread are recommended
The course passes the checkpoint at Silvergruvan (described as a checkpoint after approximately 35 km)
additional: Practical information: A bus to the 33 km start leaves Hurtigtorpet at 10:30 and must be booked in advance (booking is available until 2026-06-20); payments by methods other than card can be made to IBAN SE09 9020 0000 0906 0545 6739, using the reference number from the registration; limited pitches are available for caravans and motorhomes — please contact info@silverledenultra.se (electricity is limited); relay registration is not available in 2026; the minimum age for participants is 15 (the age they turn that year), and the 33 km race may be run under a guardian’s supervision even by younger participants; the receipt from the registration system can be used to claim a wellness allowance; equipment recommendations: trail shoes are recommended and metal studs are not; few runners use poles, but they may be recommended for the second half of the course and can be transported to the Silvergruvan checkpoint. GPX and Strava links are available; the time limit is 12 hours; there are aid stations along the course; maps and course descriptions are available on the website.

name: Muraste jooks
location: Muraste Kooli staadion, Muraste, Harku vald, Harju maakond, Estonia
description: The Muraste Run is part of the Harku Municipality Running Series and takes place on June 28, 2026, at Muraste School Stadium. The course runs along the streets and shared-use paths of Muraste, on marked, open roads. A range of distances is available for children and adults, and participants can also take part in a family competition. The top finishers in each age group will be awarded prizes, and those who complete the series will receive a season medal. The event is organized by MTÜ TreeningPluss, which promotes the joy of movement and active lifestyles.
course_highlights: The course runs along the streets and shared-use paths of Muraste
The course is marked and runs on open roads
A range of distances is available for children and adults
additional: The event centre opens at 10:00. Race materials are issued until 15 minutes before the start. The awards ceremony takes place at 13:30, with prizes for the top three men and women in each age group. The family competition is for mothers, fathers and children, who score points according to age groups. Participation is at each participant’s own risk; for minors, responsibility lies with a parent or guardian. Participation may be free or paid; exact information is unavailable. Registration is available in advance and on site, and the course runs along the streets and shared-use paths of Muraste.

name: Märgatud laps jooksmas
description: The charitable running series “Märgatud Laps jooksmas” takes place at Kose Song Festival Grounds and offers participants the chance to enjoy a sporting experience while supporting a good cause. The aim of the series is to bring the community together and offer the joy of exercise to all age groups. The event is open to everyone interested in running and creates a friendly, supportive atmosphere.
course_highlights: A supportive and friendly atmosphere throughout the running series
A charitable purpose and community involvement
Held at Kose Song Festival Grounds
additional: The run aims to involve the community and promote healthy lifestyles. Participants can support a charitable cause.

name: TrailÖvik
description: TrailÖvik is a welcoming trail race in Själevad on 28 June 2026, offering several courses (Mini, 6 km, 12 km, 22 km and Night Edition) for both recreational and elite runners. The courses pass through magnificent natural scenery, with technical single-track trails, hilly terrain and several viewpoints overlooking the High Coast World Heritage Site. The event is described as both family-friendly and professionally run, with practice runs, maps and course support. The race venue and start/finish are at Skogslöparnas clubhouse, and the race has been praised for its varied and challenging trails.
course_highlights: Magnificent scenery and views of the High Coast, including from the summit of Mycklingberget
Technical trails with steep sections, stairs up Mycklingberget and ropes at some passages
The 22 km course includes three summits, bogs, stream ravines and aid stations (sports drink and water)
additional: The race venue, start and bib-number collection are on the gravel area below Skogslöparnas clubhouse (Nordhemsvägen 41, 89430 Själevad); bibs must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start; race information will be published 10 days before the event; registration is through Mittlopp, and on-site registration opens at the venue and closes 30 minutes before each start. Practice runs and maps are available (printed maps in the mailbox at the start of Älgstråket and downloadable maps); livestreaming and live results are provided. Spiked shoes are recommended in wet weather. The 22 km course has its first aid station at approximately 4 km, with sports drink and water. Four distances and Night Edition; starts around 11:00; registration through Mittlopp; the venue is below Skogslöparnas clubhouse in Själevad (Nordhemsvägen 41); maps, practice runs and course marking are provided; results are displayed at the venue and online.

name: Böda Sandsloppet
location: Böda Sand SportCamp, Böda Sand, Öland, Sweden
description: Böda Sandsloppet is a family-friendly fun run held at Böda Sand on Öland by Högby IF Athletics. The race offers several distances for adults and young people: 6.5 km and 4 km for adults, and 1.8 km and 1 km for young people, with the start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and a highlight of the main race is a sausage after the finish. Register at olandrunning.se or on site. The registration deadline is June 26, 2026, with late registration available until July 1.
course_highlights: Forest terrain in the Böda Sand area on Öland
Distance options: 6.5 km and 4 km for adults; 1.8 km and 1 km for young people
All finishers receive a medal, and sausages are served after the finish
additional: Start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp. Registration deadline: June 26, 2026; late registration available until July 1. Register at olandrunning.se or on site. Payment by cash, card or Swish.

name: Byrundan
location: Unos Park, Gamleby, Västervik Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Byrundan is a city race held in Gamleby, starting and finishing in Unos Park. The event offers races for all ages and is well suited to both recreational runners and families. Welcome on 3 July 2026 — registration opens shortly.
course_highlights: Takes place in Gamleby’s urban setting
Starts and finishes in Unos Park
Races for all ages
additional: Registration opens shortly; start and finish in Unos Park; races are offered for all ages; organiser’s postal address: C/o Lena Persson, Lapserums Gård, 594 92 Gamleby. The race is held indoors in Unos Park; registration opens shortly for 2026-07-03.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 22. Emumäe jooks
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 brings together recreational athletes and active-lifestyle enthusiasts from spring to autumn, offering the chance to test their abilities across different age groups and distances. The 22nd Emumäe Run is the series’ fifth stage and takes place at Emumäe on 4 July. The series aims to promote running and fitness walking and support local recreational athletes. Races are held over several distances, from short children’s races to main races of up to 10 km. Timing is by chip, and race numbers must be attached to the abdomen or chest.
course_highlights: Several distances from 100 m to 10 km, suitable for different age groups
Chip timing; race numbers must be attached to the abdomen or chest
The series stages take place at various locations in Lääne-Virumaa; the Emumäe Run is the fifth stage
additional: Pre-registration is available on the running series website and closes at 16:00 on the day before the race. On-site registration takes place at the times specified in the race guide. No points are awarded in the youngest distance categories (Tillujooks, Minijooks, Lastejooks). Chips are attached to the back of the race number and covered with foam board; they must not be removed. The running series features various distances and categories, welcomes a diverse range of participants, and aims to promote a healthy lifestyle and bring the community together.

name: Võhma terviseraja maraton
location: Võhma, Põhja-Sakala vald, Viljandi County, Estonia
description: The Võhma Health Trail Marathon is a trail marathon held on the Võhma city health trail. The course is a 620-metre loop to be completed 68 times, for a total of 42.2 km. The race takes place on 4 July 2026, starting at 9:00, and offers participants a medal, timekeeping, course support, food at the finish, and washing facilities. In addition to the marathon, participants can also run a shorter distance for free, without their time being recorded; this option is suitable for anyone who enjoys being active.
course_highlights: 620-metre loop on the health trail
68 laps for the marathon distance (42.2 km)
Trail terrain
additional: Race-day packet pick-up starts at 8:00. The number of participants is limited. From 9:00 to 13:00, runners wishing to cover a shorter distance than 42 km are allowed on the course; participation is free and times are not recorded. Everyone who completes at least 17 laps (10.5 km) receives a medal. The marathon is open to active participants born in 2010 or earlier. Timekeeping is manual. The time limit is 6 hours 30 minutes. The entry fee includes a medal, timekeeping, course support, food at the finish, and washing facilities. The entry fee can be paid in cash on race day or in advance to a bank account. Previous marathon winners may participate for free. Trail terrain, registration by email, limited number of participants, medal and services included in the entry fee

name: J. Lossmanni mälestusjooks
description: The Jüri Lossmann Memorial Run is a traditional running event held in Viljandi. The event takes place on 4 July 2026, starting at 19:00. The run is dedicated to Jüri Lossmann and offers participants the chance to enjoy a pleasant summer evening and a sporting challenge.
course_highlights: Location in the city of Viljandi
Evening start at 19:00
Traditional memorial run
additional: The run takes place in the evening and is part of the traditions of Estonia’s running community, offering participants the chance to remember and celebrate.

name: Kolmårdsrundan / Kolmården Ultra Trail

description: Kolmården Ultra Trail is a welcoming but demanding trail race for both elite runners and recreational runners. Choose between the longer challenges (45 km or 60 km), with routes taking you through Kolmården Forest, up onto Kvarseboklint’s mountain ridge and down to the shore of Bråviken, onward past the natural surroundings of Nävsjön, and finally through the technical Bråviksbranten before the finish. The race combines technical trails, boardwalks across bogs and spectacular views, with well-equipped aid stations along the way. The organizer emphasizes safety and mandatory equipment, as well as a medal and light refreshments at the finish.
course_highlights: Kvarseboklint’s impressive mountain ridge with views
Descent to the shore of Bråviken and passage by Nävsjön, with boardwalks across vast bogs
Technical and demanding running through the Bråviksbranten Nature Reserve
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, running vest/backpack with fluids (at least 0.5 L), pressure bandage/blood-stopping dressing, and a map with the emergency number (provided at bib collection). Aid stations: 45K = 4; 60K = 5 (detailed stations with different energy products are listed for the 48 km variant). Bib collection from 05:30; bibs must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start. The course is marked with large orange arrows and flagging tape. Light refreshments and a custom-designed medal are included at the finish; massage is available at cost. Energy and fluids provided in partnership with Umara. Mandatory equipment; start times: 45K 08:00; cutoff time 13:30 at 44 km; aid stations: 45K = 4, 60K = 5; finish: a meal is included in the entry fee.

name: Mörksuggejakten TrailRun
description: Mörksuggejakten is a classic race in the long-distance cycling cup in Rättvik, enjoyed by elite cyclists and recreational riders alike. The main course is available as a 72 km route or a shortened 44 km version, featuring varied terrain with gravel roads, trails and some challenging climbs, as well as fine views over Siljan. The route passes places such as Vidablick, the Hedsåsen summer farm, the Enån valley with its narrow suspension bridges, and Dalhalla and Springkällan. The event also includes Lilla Mörksuggejakten for young riders at the Jarl area and is organised by IK Jarl.
course_highlights: Main course: 72 km (or a shorter 44 km option)
Views over Siljan from Vidablick and the Hedsåsen summer farm
Sections along the Enån valley with narrow suspension bridges; passes Dalhalla and Springkällan
additional: Registration for race categories is via RaceWeb; late registration is handled on RaceWeb between 08:30 and 12:00 (Lilla Mörksuggan). Bib collection for Lilla Mörksuggan: Jarlstugan, Saturday 5 July, 09:00–11:30. Bibs with chips are used in race categories and recreational/family categories (children's, recreational/family categories are not timed). A technical zone/feeding station is located in the arena between the start and finish zones; medical staff will be on site (contact person: Josefin Linell, tel. 076-796 39 69). Changing rooms and showers are available at Jarlstugan. Mörksuggejakten TrailRun was first held in 2017. The race is part of the Mörksuggejakten events in Rättvik and is coordinated with Lilla Mörksuggejakten; late registration and bib collection are planned in connection with 4 July 2026.

name: Semesterhalvmaran
location: Fjugesta, Laxå Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: The Vacation Half Marathon is a summer race organized by running club LK Gränslöst, giving runners the opportunity to experience the beautiful open landscapes of the Närke Plain. The course often follows gravel roads among rolling grain fields, offering a nature-close, summery running experience. LK Gränslöst is an inclusive club that welcomes runners of all levels.
course_highlights: Gravel roads across the Närke Plain
Rolling grain fields and open views
A summer vacation-time race with a relaxed, nature-close feel
additional: LK Gränslöst organizes several summer races: the Vacation Half Marathon, the Summer Ten-Kilometer, and the children’s race Solruset. The club announced that the races would be paused in 2025 because key people in the organizing group were unavailable. The club also holds open Wednesday training sessions at 18:00 in Örebro (location varies), led by Carina Gustavsson and Thomas Stenius.

name: Gotland Run 511k (2026)
description: Gotland Run 511k is more of a running adventure than a traditional race: a self-supported journey around Gotland of approximately 511 km, starting and finishing in Visby. Participants follow a clockwise loop that also includes a circuit of Fårö, with support from four so-called Angel Stations along the way. The organizer provides some basic services, but runners are responsible for most food and logistics arrangements. The entire route must be completed on foot within 10 days, with regular position reports throughout the day.
course_highlights: Circular route around Gotland (starting and finishing in Visby), including a circuit of Fårö
Most of the route follows Gotlandsleden: long stretches of asphalt, gravel roads, and shorter sections of trail
Four Angel Stations along the course offering water, support, and sometimes the opportunity for a short rest or a bed
additional: Self-supported format: the organizer provides only the most basic services; participants are responsible for food and most accommodation. A pre-race dinner and race briefing in Visby on the evening before the start are mandatory. One night’s accommodation at Visby Fängelse Hostel and breakfast on race morning are included, as are a race bib, luggage storage during the race, and a souvenir for finishers. Transport back to Visby is available for participants who withdraw. Participants must report their position twice daily (10:00 and 22:00) using an online check-in tool and a Google Maps link. The overall time limit is 10 days (an average of ~51 km per day). The information page has sections on mandatory equipment and basic rules. History: the first edition in 2023 had 5 starters and 3 finishers. Distance approximately 511 km (318 miles); four Angel Stations along the way; no pacing; mandatory equipment; pre-race dinner and briefing; one night’s accommodation in Visby included; luggage storage; race bib; transport back to Visby if withdrawing; finishers receive a souvenir.

name: 6. Navi jooksu-kõnnitiir
description: The Võrumaa Running and Walking Series is a multi-stage series of running and walking events, offering a range of distances for adults and children. The main distances are approximately 5 to 8 kilometres, and the course runs mainly on asphalt and gravel roads, with a short section on soft ground. The series also includes mini distances and children’s runs suitable for all age groups. The events take place in various locations across Võrumaa, giving participants the opportunity to enjoy the region’s beautiful nature and sporting community.
course_highlights: Main distances of 5–8 km, mainly on asphalt and gravel roads
Mini distances and children’s runs suitable for all age groups
The course passes through scenic natural areas in Võrumaa and includes some soft terrain
additional: The series offers several distances: the main distance, a shorter distance, a mini distance, a walk, and a children’s run. The course is mostly paved with asphalt; the mini distances and children’s runs also take place on asphalt. Detailed course maps and instructions are available for the individual stages. Timed-run results are available through Nelson Timing. The series also includes a family and friends team category, and participant numbers can be tracked across seasons. The Võrumaa Running and Walking Series comprises multiple stages and distances, held on different dates and at various locations in the Võrumaa region. Entry fees and registration information are below.

name: Navi jooksutiir
description: Navi Run is a running, Nordic walking, and walking event held in Võru County and organized by Navi Village Association. The event offers an opportunity to enjoy exercise and a healthy lifestyle in beautiful natural surroundings, and is suitable for participants of different ability levels. The run is part of a broader initiative to promote recreational exercise, with the aim of supporting an active and healthy lifestyle. Everyone who enjoys being active is invited to enjoy a sporting day and the pleasure of movement.
course_highlights: Beautiful natural surroundings in Võru County
Varied terrain suitable for running, Nordic walking, and walking
Organized by Navi Village Association
additional: An opportunity to take part in different distances; registration and results are online, and the event is part of the wider Võrumaa running and walking series.

name: Västervik City Run
description: Västervik City Run is a 6.2 km city race in and around central Västervik, starting and finishing at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget. The course consists of two loops of approximately 3 km, with the lap point at Fiskaretorget. The race has been held since 2011 and traditionally takes place on the Monday of week 28, starting at 20:00. It is well established in Västervik and attracts runners of different ages.
course_highlights: 6.2 km city race (two loops of approximately 3 km)
Start and finish at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget
Lap point at Fiskaretorget
additional: The children’s race (Sparbanksloppet) is an 800 m fun run for children up to age 10, with a group start from Fiskaretorget at 18:30. The children’s race starts level with the Stegeholm Castle ruins, by the sun deck and Myntbryggan, and follows the cycle path along Gamlebyviken to the finish at Grönsakstorget. Participants receive a medal after finishing. Bib collection is at ICA Maxi or the race office; advance registration closes on 3 July at 16:00; registration on race day is open from 13:00 to 19:00.

name: Kambja Tervisejooksud
description: Kambja Health Runs is a three-stage running series that invites both recreational and experienced runners to enjoy active time outdoors. At each stage, participants can choose between a loop of the approximately 5 km health trail and a 10 km race. There is also an exciting power run to determine the best strength-to-speed ratio. Series finishers are eligible for prizes and prize draws, including the grand prize of a bicycle. Participation is free, and registration is available online or on site.
course_highlights: Approximately 5 km health-trail loop
10 km race starts at 18:00
Power run to determine the strength-to-speed ratio
additional: The start is open from 18:00 to 20:00; the 10 km race starts at 18:00, and the finish closes at 21:00. Prizes will be drawn among everyone who participates in at least two stages. The grand prize—a bicycle—will be drawn among everyone who finishes all three stages. Everyone who finishes all three stages will receive a series T-shirt. Participation is free, and registration is available online or on site. The series is part of the Tartumaa Running and Walking Series. Participants can register online or on site; participation is free, and prizes, including a bicycle, will be drawn as part of the series. This is part of the Tartumaa Running and Walking Series.

name: 7. ETAPP
description: Käime Koos is a recreational sports series by the Estonian Sports Association Kalev, inviting participants to take part in various hiking and walking stages across Estonia. The 7th stage takes place on Kesselaid, offering participants the chance to enjoy the beautiful natural scenery of the Muhu escarpment. The series aims to promote physical activity and a healthy lifestyle through hiking and walking together. Participants can experience varied terrain and combine exercise with good company.
course_highlights: Beautiful natural scenery of the Muhu escarpment
Varied terrain suitable for walking and hiking
The series takes place in different parts of Estonia, showcasing local natural beauty
additional: Käime Koos stages take place in different locations across Estonia, where participants can enjoy nature and physical activity. The series is organised by the Estonian Sports Association Kalev. More information and contact: Sirje Soovik +372 506 2250.

name: 31. Joosu Järvejooksu sarja 4. etapp
location: Tervise- ja suusarada, Viljandi, Viljandi County, Estonia
description: The 4th stage of the Joosu Lake Run series is a running race around Lake Viljandi on the health and ski trail. The race is part of the traditional Joosu series, offering participants the chance to enjoy beautiful nature and varied terrain. The course has a good surface and is suitable for runners of different abilities. The event is organised by Tervisespordiklubi Joosu, which welcomes all running enthusiasts to take part.
course_highlights: Health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi
Beautiful nature and varied terrain
Good running surface suitable for different ability levels
additional: The race takes place around Lake Viljandi, probably in nature or on roads, and is part of a wider sports event in 2026.

name: Vooremäe tipujooks
description: Vooremäe Summit Run is a running competition organized by the Tartumaa Sports Association and held at Vooremäe. It is a traditional summer sporting event that welcomes running enthusiasts and offers the chance to enjoy beautiful nature and a sporting competition. The event is part of Tartumaa’s sports calendar and is suitable for runners of different abilities.
course_highlights: The competition takes place in the Vooremäe terrain
Beautiful natural scenery and views along the course
Suitable for runners of different abilities
additional: The event is part of the Tartumaa running and health-walking series and focuses on trail running at Vooremäe, offering recreational sport and an opportunity to get active in nature.

name: Nordansjö Nattultra
location: Norbergs OK:s klubbstuga, Nordansjö 24, Norberg, Sweden
description: Nordansjö Nattultra is a nature-focused ultrarunning experience taking place on the night of 10–11 July 2026, with the main 60 km race consisting of five loops. The race is organised by Norbergs OK, starting and finishing at the club’s cabin in Nordansjö. It is suitable for both experienced ultrarunners and runners looking to try a longer summer challenge. The course is easy to run and designed to offer an enjoyable summer experience combining camaraderie and competition. A warm welcome to the second edition of Nordansjö Nattultra!
course_highlights: Five loops of 12 km each (60 km total)
Mainly right-of-way roads/gravel roads, plus approximately 2.7 km on an illuminated trail
The course is run clockwise and includes a descent down Håberget five times
additional: Mandatory equipment: headlamp and mobile phone. The time limit for 60 km is 10 hours; runners finish after five loops (5×12 km). Race bibs can be collected from 19:00 on Friday 10 July at the club cabin. Aid stations are located at the start/finish and halfway around the course (6 km); no disposable cups are provided—bring your own soft flask or cup. Finishers receive a finisher cap, medal and breakfast at the club cabin. Maximum 100 starters (first come, first served). Håberget mountain prize; start/finish at Norbergs OK’s club cabin in Nordansjö (Nordansjö 24, Norberg); maximum 100 participants; aid stations at the start, finish and halfway; no cups are provided—bring your own cup; registration opened 2025-09-01.

name: 45. jooks ümber Pühajärve
location: Pühajärve Spa & Holiday Resort, Otepää, Valga County, Estonia
description: The 45th Run Around Lake Pühajärv is a traditional running race held around Pühajärv Spa & Holiday Resort. The distance is 10.7 km, and the course is well marked and secured, offering participants beautiful views of the lake. The race is part of the 2026 Maru Lake Runs series and is its third event. The start is at 12:00 on Saturday, July 11. Participants are provided with timing, refreshment stations and an awards ceremony.
course_highlights: A 10.7 km course around Lake Pühajärv
Refreshment stations at 4.4 km and 7.7 km
The course is marked and secured by course marshals
additional: Start groups are formed based on previous results; elite runners may start in the first group. Timing is chip-based, with the chip attached to the back of the race bib. Participants receive a medal, sports drink and water on the course and at the finish, as well as medical assistance along the entire course. The awards ceremony is scheduled for approximately 13:30, with awards for the top six. Participants can register on site, and discounts are available. The course runs around Lake Pühajärv and is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners.

name: Sportland Kõrvemaa Triatlon 2026
location: Kõrvemaa Matka- ja Suusakeskus, Kõrvemaa, Estonia
description: Sportland Kõrvemaa Triathlon takes place on 11 July 2026 at Kõrvemaa Hiking and Ski Centre and offers an exciting recreational triathlon experience. The main distance consists of a 250 m swim, a 20 km mountain-bike ride and a 4 km run, which runs largely along the ski trails and forest roads of the Põhja-Kõrvemaa Landscape Protection Area. In addition to the main event, participants can take part in the Stebby duathlon and youth duathlon, which are intended for different age groups. The event is well organised, with chip timing, medical support and aid stations. After the race, participants receive a medal and can enjoy hot soup, a sauna and bike washing facilities.
course_highlights: The swim takes place in the pond at Kõrvemaa Hiking and Ski Centre; one lap, with a maximum depth of 2.5 m
The 20 km cycling course follows the ski trails and forest roads of the Põhja-Kõrvemaa Landscape Protection Area
The 4 km trail run is marked and secured
additional: Starts are staggered in waves of five, with a 10-second interval between each start. Competitors must wear a helmet while cycling and a timing chip around their ankle. The entry fee includes medical first aid, aid-station service, a medal, hot soup, a smoothie, access to a sauna and hot tub, and bike washing. There is a bag drop at the event centre and a place to change clothes in the sauna anteroom. The swim number must be written on the cheek or shoulder with a waterproof marker. Drafting is allowed during the cycling leg. Trail course, family races, free soup and sauna, registration information, entry fees vary, limited number of places

name: Mõisa jooks
location: Mäetaguse mõisa piirkond, Mäetaguse, Ida-Viru County, Estonia
organizer: SK Team Kehtna ja Alutaguse vallavalitsus
price_range: 10.- for main race, 8.- for youth, 3.- for children
description: The Kehtna Manor Run is a friendly, community-focused running event held in the area around Kehtna Manor. It offers three distances: a 5 km main race, a 2.5 km youth race, and a 500 m children’s race, suitable for participants of different ages. In addition to the races, the event features Children’s Day activities, pony rides, and trampolines, creating a pleasant family-day atmosphere. It is organized by SK Team Kehtna, which is committed to promoting sport and physical activity in the community.
course_highlights: 5 km main race
2.5 km youth race
500 m children’s race
additional: The event center opens at 11:00. The children’s race starts at 12:00, and the youth and main races start at 12:15. The awards ceremony takes place at 13:00. After the races, there are Children’s Day activities, pony rides, and trampolines. The races take place in July and include various age groups and distance options; registration is available on the website; the event includes activities for children and lists the start times.

name: 5. Pühajärve pargimiil
location: Pühajärve Spa & Holiday Resort, Otepää, Valga County, Estonia
description: The 5th Pühajärve Park Mile is a 1.6 km running race held in the park of Pühajärve Holiday Centre on Saturday, 11 July 2026. The start and finish are at the same location, and the race begins at 12:10. The race is open to all running enthusiasts and offers a pleasant opportunity to enjoy a run in beautiful park surroundings. Participants receive a medal and race bib, chip timing, sports drink and water at the finish, and medical assistance along the entire course.
course_highlights: The marked course is one mile, or 1.6 km long
The start and finish are in the park of Pühajärve Holiday Centre
Sports drink and water are available at the finish
additional: Race bibs will be distributed on race day from 9:30 to 11:45. Timing is by a chip attached to the back of the race bib. Participants receive a medal and race bib, timing, a result in the final results, services, sports drink, and water at the finish. Medical assistance is available along the entire course. Parking is provided in a separate car park, just past Pühajärve Holiday Centre on the right when arriving from the direction of Otepää. The race takes place in the park of Pühajärve Holiday Centre, with the start and finish at the same location. The event is part of the local running calendar and offers an opportunity to enjoy nature and experience a friendly community atmosphere.

name: Pajusi Mudajooks
organizer: MTÜ Sporty ja MTÜ Pajusi Küla Selts
description: Pajusi Mud Run is a popular mass-participation sporting event in Central Estonia, offering participants an exciting and adventurous obstacle course of up to 10 km. The event takes place on 11 July 2026 in Pajusi village and is suitable for both individual runners and teams. The course features natural and man-made obstacles that test participants’ physical and mental endurance. Separate courses are available for children, and all finishers receive a commemorative medal. Free parking and hot soup after the run are provided for participants.
course_highlights: A course of up to 10 km through Central Estonia’s varied natural landscape
Natural and man-made obstacles along the course
Separate courses for children and young people
additional: The main race starts together from the Pajusi Village House. Shoes that could damage the obstacles, such as shoes with spikes or sharp elements, are not permitted on the course. All finishers receive a commemorative medal. Hot soup is available for participants, and food is also offered by vendors on site. Free, unattended parking is available near the start area. Participant names and personal identification codes, as well as a team name, can be added to the ticket. The name on a ticket can be changed until 30 June 2026. Participants can choose from different categories, including courses for children and young people. The event takes place on 11 July 2026, with additional on-site services including food and drinks, and medals for finishers.

name: Musköloppet
location: Muskö Hembygdsgård, Muskö, Haninge kommun, Stockholms län, Sverige
description: Musköloppet is a long-standing running race in a spectacular archipelago setting, starting and finishing at Muskö Local Heritage Centre/Muskö IF’s clubhouse. The race usually attracts around 300 runners (about 400 including the youngest children) and has a friendly, homecoming atmosphere, with many taking the opportunity to meet relatives and neighbours. The event offers children’s and youth classes as well as recreational classes (5 km and 10 km) on varied surfaces, and takes place on Saturday, 11 July 2026.
course_highlights: Start/finish at Muskö Local Heritage Centre, near the clubhouse, outdoor gym and hockey rink
Course surfaces: approximately 50% asphalt, 30–40% gravel and 10% trail
