The 5 km and 10 km courses are officially measured (course measurer Mikael Hill, 240523); this year, the 10 km is run as a single loop
additional: Late registration is available at the start/finish area up to one hour before the race starts. Food and drinks are available at the start/finish. Directions by car and public transport, as well as parking information, are available on the “Find us” page. Around 300 runners usually take part (about 400 including the youngest children). Start/finish area at Muskö Local Heritage Centre/Muskö IF’s clubhouse; 5 km and 10 km courses with varied surfaces (approximately 50% asphalt, 40% gravel and 10% trail on one course; approximately 60% asphalt, 30% gravel and 10% trail on the other); merchandise, kiosk snacks, coffee, soft drinks and food from Micke’s Grill; late registration at the finish area up to one hour before the race starts.

name: Lidingöloppet Funäsfjällen
description: Lidingöloppet in Funäsfjällen is “Sweden’s most beautiful challenge” — a trail race featuring steep climbs, sloping trails, open meadows and sweeping mountain views. The third edition takes place on 11 July 2026, offering an unbeatable combination of adrenaline and nature experiences. Welcome to Bruksvallarna Ski Stadium. Register via the Lidingöloppet website and collect your race bib at the venue.
course_highlights: Steep climbs and challenging mountain terrain
Sloping trails and flat meadows
Sweeping mountain views and panoramic vistas
additional: Registration is via the Lidingöloppet website; race bibs are collected at the venue in Bruksvallarna. A 100 kr fee applies to registrations made on race day (Saturday). The week before the race, Bruksvallarnas Running Week features shoe testing, running clinics, children’s activities, after-run events and an expo at Arena Syd outside Bruksvallarnas Sportcenter. Results become official and final one week after the race. By registering, you agree to have your name published in start and results lists and to images being used in the event’s channels; requests for exceptions are handled by the event office (info@lidingoloppet.se). Seeding and start times; accommodation in Ramundberget near the start; logistical facilities such as parking, water stations, and food and drink; a week in July with programme and accommodation information at bruksvallsliden.se/lidingoloppet; children’s race/adventure for younger participants

name: PALMS Südasuve Challenge - Võsu 2026
location: Võsu, Lääne-Nigula vald, Lääne County, Estonia
description: PALMS Midsummer Challenge - Võsu 2026 is a sporting summer event held in the town of Võsu. It is an enjoyable and active challenge for running enthusiasts, offering the chance to enjoy summer nature and community support. The event is part of the Estonian Night Run series and brings together runners from different regions. Võsu’s beautiful coastal scenery provides excellent conditions for a sporting experience.
course_highlights: Coastal scenery in the town of Võsu
A pleasant, active summer running environment
Part of the Estonian Night Run series
additional: The event includes a range of swimming distances and is open to both local and virtual participants, offering summer sea air and sport in a friendly atmosphere.

name: Vimka tõusu maraton
description: Vimka tõusu marathon is a summer marathon on the Viimsi Peninsula, offering participants one large loop. The start and finish are located in the parking lot of Randvere School. The varied course includes both paved roads and forest trails, with several climbs and descents that make the run exciting and varied.
course_highlights: One large loop on the Viimsi Peninsula
Varied course with asphalt and forest trails
The course includes climbs and descents
additional: 64 loops, each approximately 666 m; approximately 40 m of elevation gain per loop; varied terrain; one refreshment point; official chip timing; results in the statistics platform marathon100.com

name: Võru kergejõustikuõhtu
location: Võru Staadion, Võru, Võru County, Estonia
description: The Võru Athletics Evenings series is a traditional series of athletics events combining throwing, jumping, and running disciplines. The series consists of several stages, where participants can compete in different distances and events, with the IAAF scoring tables used to determine rankings. Competitions take place at Võru Stadium and are open to athletes of varying abilities. The series offers a varied athletics experience for both recreational and advanced athletes.
course_highlights: Combines throwing, jumping, and running disciplines
Multi-stage series at Võru Stadium
Uses the IAAF scoring tables to determine rankings
additional: Registration usually opens in May. Separate registration is required for each stage. Registration for throwing and jumping events usually closes at 16:30, and for running events at 18:30. Participants receive a race number that is valid for the whole season. The competition schedule includes exact registration and event times; for example, registration for the long jump and discus throw closes at 16:45, and attempts begin at 17:00. Competitions take place at Võru Stadium. Information about the multiple stages, different athletics events, registration, and schedule is available.

name: Lüllemäe mägedejooks
description: The Lüllemäe Mountain Run is the third stage of the Valgamaa running series and takes place on the Lüllemäe health trails. The main race is 4.5 km, with tiny and mini races for children also held at the Lüllemäe Basic School stadium. The event is suitable for runners of different ages and offers the chance to enjoy beautiful nature and a sporting atmosphere. Children’s races are free, and the main race entry fees are reasonable, encouraging broad participation.
course_highlights: 4.5 km main race on the Lüllemäe health trails
Children’s tiny and mini races at the stadium, over distances from 100 m to 900 m
The event takes place in a beautiful natural setting in Valgamaa
additional: There is no entry fee for the children’s races. The NM18 age group in the main race is also free. Entry fees are paid in cash on site. For event information, call +372 5202962. Trail run on local terrain; registration at www.timesport.ee; free entry for children and the NM18 group.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 9. Rakvere valla Suvejooks
location: Kooli 4, Rakvere, Rakvere vald, Lääne-Virumaa, Estonia
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 is a multi-stage running and walking series featuring various races in the Lääne-Virumaa region. The 9th stage, Rakvere Municipality Summer Run, takes place on 18 July 2026 in Rakvere at Kooli 4. The series aims to offer running enthusiasts a sporting challenge and enjoyment, while promoting an active lifestyle throughout the region.
course_highlights: Varied terrain, including sports fields and cycle paths
Various distances and age categories
Large number of participants and community involvement
additional: Participants receive medals, and the results are officially published online; registration takes place through the website.

name: Väinjärve jooks , 8. Järvamaa Järvede jooksud VI etapp
description: The Järvamaa Lakes Runs is a traditional running series consisting of several stages held by different lakes in Järvamaa. The Väinjärv Run, taking place on 18 July 2026, is the sixth stage of the series. The race offers participants the chance to enjoy the beautiful natural surroundings and varied terrain around the lake. The series offers several distances and is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners.
course_highlights: Runs take place by different lakes in Järvamaa
Varied terrain and beautiful natural surroundings
The sixth stage of a traditional running series, held by Väinjärv
additional: The races take place around Väinjärv and include several distances, including 400 m, 1.2 km and 4.6 km. Pre-registration is recommended to secure your participation.

name: Ümber Väinjärve jooks
description: The Run Around Lake Väinjärv is a traditional running event held around the beautiful Lake Väinjärv. It is part of the Väinjärv Water Festival sports programme, where sport and fun go hand in hand. Everyone is welcome to enjoy the natural surroundings of the lake and take on a sporting challenge. The Water Festival also features other sports and activities offering entertainment for participants of all ages.
course_highlights: Beautiful surroundings of Lake Väinjärv
Traditional running event around the lake
Suitable for all running enthusiasts
additional: The run is part of a wider sports programme that also includes swimming, a canoe rally, beach volleyball, a darts competition, beach football and children's sports competitions. The event is a traditional, entertaining occasion for athletes and families alike. Participants register on site. The event is part of a larger water festival and sports programme, featuring various sports and activities, and participation is free. Registration is already open for beach volleyball and beach football teams.

name: Rakvere valla suvejooks
description: The Rakvere Municipality Summer Run is a traditional running race held in the Sõmeru area. It is part of the Lääne-Virumaa Running and Walking Series and offers a sporting challenge for running enthusiasts. The courses are varied and suitable for runners of different levels. The race is friendly and community-oriented, welcoming all running enthusiasts.
course_highlights: Varied terrain in the Sõmeru area
Suitable for runners of different levels
Part of the Lääne-Virumaa Running and Walking Series
additional: The race takes place at the Sõmeru-Näpi recreational sports field and is part of a local series of sporting events that brings together stages of the running and walking series.

name: Helags Fjällmara
distance_verbose: Marathon, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3000 meter, 0.8 km
description: Helags Fjällmara is a classic mountain trail race in the Ljungdalsfjällen, held since 1985. The event offers several distances for different levels, from a children’s race to longer mountain trail races, with beautiful views and challenging trails. The start and finish are in the meadow in the centre of Ljungdalen, creating a welcoming race venue for both elite runners and families. The event is organised by volunteers from Ljungdalens Gymnastik och Idrottsförening.
course_highlights: Mountain terrain with beautiful views and challenging trails
Start and finish in the meadow in Ljungdalen
Several distances for different levels (23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m)
additional: Practical information: registration is open until 16/7 (no on-site late registration); registration for the children’s race is open until 18/7 at 10:15. Participant limits: 23 km 250 participants, 12 km 200, 5 km 150, 3 km 100, 800 m 200. The entry fee includes energy and water stations along the course, a personal cup from Umara (bring it during the race), electronic timing (chip in the race bib) and a medal for everyone who finishes. Showers and a sauna are available after the finish. Registration is binding; transferring an entry and changing category are possible for a change fee of 250 kr (changes are made as instructed by email; the registration page lists both info@ljungdalensgif.se and hej@helagsfjallmara.se as contacts). Competition categories for elite runners, recreational runners and children; registration takes place via raceweb on the website; several distances are available: 42 km, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m.

name: Hornsjön Runt
location: Pensionat Hornsjön, Löttorp, Borgholm Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Hornsjön Runt is a family-friendly running event around Öland’s only inland lake, through beautiful and varied scenery. Organised by Högby IF, it offers distances for children and young people, 5.5 km, 11 km, and a non-timed walking class. The start and finish are at Pensionat Hornsjön, and everyone who completes the event receives a medal. The event combines a long tradition with scenic routes over gravel, sand dunes, forest, and open pastures.
course_highlights: Around Öland’s only inland lake (Hornsjön)
Varied terrain: gravel with Öland limestone, grass, and sand dunes
Passes cow pastures and deciduous and coniferous forest; three water stations along the course
additional: Register by 11 July 2026. Late registration is available through 16 July, followed by the option to register when race bibs are distributed from 12:00 on race day. The non-timed walking class starts between 13:00 and 16:00. There are three water stations along the course, plus refreshments at the start/finish. Showers and changing facilities are available at Högby sports ground. Prizes are awarded to the top three in all classes, with additional prizes drawn at random. Start times: youth classes 15:30; 5.5 km 17:00; 11 km 17:05. The walking class is available over 5.5 or 11 km, with starts between 13:00 and 16:00. Showers and changing facilities are available at Högby sports ground.

name: 31. Jooks-kõnd ümber Uhtjärve
location: Uhtjärve Ürgoru Nõiariik OÜ, Uhtjärve, Võrumaa, Estonia
description: The 31st Run-Walk Around Lake Uhtjärv is a traditional running and walking series in the Võru County region, offering a variety of distance options for everyone. The event takes place in the beautiful natural surroundings of Lake Uhtjärv, providing a sporting challenge for both runners and walkers. The series includes various distances and mini distances suitable for beginners and experienced athletes alike. The event is part of the Võru County running and walking series, known for its friendly atmosphere and good organization.
course_highlights: Beautiful natural surroundings around Lake Uhtjärv
A variety of distances for runners and walkers
Suitable for beginners and experienced athletes alike
additional: The event center opens at 11:00 at the Kubija Ski Base. Buses depart from Kubija for Haanja and Kasaritsa, where the starts are located. In addition to the main distance, the series includes shorter distances, mini distances, and a walking option. A children's run is also held as part of the series. The event takes place on July 19, 2026, and includes running and walking around Lake Uhtjärv. Participants can choose from different distances and enjoy nature and sport.

name: Jooks ümber Uhtjärve
description: The Võrumaa Running and Walking Series is a multi-stage series of running and walking events offering a range of distances for both adults and children. The main distances are approximately 5 to 8 kilometres, and the course runs mainly on asphalt and gravel roads, with some off-road sections. The series also includes mini distances and toddler runs suitable for all age groups. The event is open to everyone interested in sport and promotes healthy lifestyles and community involvement.
course_highlights: The main distances run mainly on asphalt and gravel roads
The 8 km course around Lake Vaskna also includes softer ground on the grounds of the Haanja Recreation and Sports Centre
Mini distances and toddler runs take place on both asphalt and soft ground
additional: The series offers different distances: the main distance, a shorter distance, a mini distance and a toddler run. The course is mostly paved with asphalt, but also includes gravel and off-road sections. Walking options are also available on longer and shorter distances. Participants earn points in a season standings table, with separate rankings for families and groups of friends. Event centres and starts are held at different locations, such as Kubija Ski Base and the Haanja Suur Muna café. Bus transport to the start locations is arranged. There are multiple distances and stages; advance registration is required, and participation fees are listed in the registration form.

name: Runmaröloppen 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Mini-Lunken 1.5km 60kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och en kula glass.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lunken 5.7km: från 150kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Halvmarathon 21km: från 350kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

description: RUNmaröloppen is a family-friendly race in the heart of the Stockholm archipelago on Runmarö, starting and finishing at the Svängen inn. The event offers short children’s races, Lunken (5.7 km) and a half marathon (21 km) along beautiful trails, open fields and through archipelago villages—perfect for a day trip by Waxholmsbolaget boats. The races have limited participant numbers and place great emphasis on atmosphere, aid stations and sustainability; 20% of the surplus goes to the Archipelago Foundation.
course_highlights: Half marathon (21 km) around the whole of Runmarö, with views towards Sandhamn
A mix of trail paths, gravel roads and archipelago villages; two trail sections on the half marathon
Permanent course signs and 1 km markers on the half marathon, as well as many local aid stations
additional: Start and finish at the Svängen inn (about 400 m from the pier). Mini-Lunken starts at 11:00; Lunken and the Half Marathon start at 13:00. The half marathon has 1 km markers, an interactive map, a total elevation gain of 169 m and several local refreshment stations (for example, Nore with pickled cucumber and Solberga). Mini-Lunken participants get an ice cream; everyone receives a medal and a post-race drink. Race entries are limited (200 places for the half marathon and 120 for Lunken in the first release, with a further 30 places released closer to race day, often at 18:00 the day before). Registration opens on 1 May at 09:00. 20% of the surplus is donated to the Archipelago Foundation. Results are published online and the awards ceremony takes place after the races; in the evening, there is dinner and a party at Svängen. Start and finish at Svängen; courses marked; registration opens 1 May at 09:00; places are limited (200 for the Half Marathon, 120 for Lunken in the first release, plus 30 additional places later); a strong charitable focus and local atmosphere.

name: Aastajooks
organizer: Spordiklubi Pärnu Kahe Silla Klubi MTÜ
description: Pärnu Annual Runs is a traditional running series that began in 1985 and is inspired by the Eastern calendar, dedicating each year to that year’s symbolic animal. The theme of the 2026 running series is the Year of the Fire Horse. It consists of nine stages held in three different areas of Pärnu: Vallikäär, Pärnu Beach, and the Reiu-Raeküla health trail. Three stages take place at each location, offering participants a varied and enjoyable running experience. The series aims to provide a sporting challenge and enjoyment for both recreational and experienced runners.
course_highlights: 9 stages divided among 3 starting locations: Pärnu Vallikäär, Pärnu Beach, and the Reiu-Raeküla health trail
3 stages at each starting location, for a total of 9 runs during the season
The running series theme is inspired by the Eastern calendar and dedicated to that year’s symbolic animal
additional: The series includes 9 stages divided among three different starting locations. Each stage starts at 18:00. Participants can purchase a season pass or register for individual stages. The organizers also welcome volunteers and offer gift cards. Several stages and different distances are available, including 1500 m at Vallikäär, 3000 m at the beach, and 5000 m at Reiu-Raeküla; the event takes place on 21 July 2026 in Pärnu.

name: Kohila Pikamaajooksusari
description: The Kohila Distance Running Series is a race series for sports enthusiasts in Kohila Parish, offering a variety of running opportunities for different age and ability groups. The series aims to promote recreational exercise and provide participants with an enjoyable sporting experience. Participants receive a commemorative medal at each stage, and points are tallied for the overall series standings. The series is organised by Kohila Sports Centre, which offers modern facilities and a strong sporting environment.
course_highlights: A range of running distances for different age groups
Points tally and commemorative medals at every stage
Organised at Kohila Sports Centre’s modern stadium and track
additional: All participants receive a commemorative medal at every stage. Points are tallied in each competition class for the overall series standings. Registration is available online at www.kohilaseeriajooksud.ee or by email and phone. Kohila Sports Centre offers a modern stadium and sports facilities, including a 400 m running track, spectator stands and a car park. The series consists of nine stages, during which participants collect points to determine the overall winners. Competitions take place at Kohila Stadium and are open to different age groups.

name: KEVEK ja Tartu Kalev staadionijooksu sari
description: The KEVEK and Tartu Kalev Stadium Running Series is a series of races organized by Tartu Sports Society Kalev and held in the city of Tartu. The series consists of several stages, offering opportunities to take part in track races across different age groups. Competitions are held mainly at Tamme and Ülenurme Stadiums and are aimed at both young people and adults, providing a friendly sporting environment. Registration closes at 12:00 on race day, offering flexibility for participants.
course_highlights: Competitions take place at Tartu Tamme and Ülenurme Stadiums
The series includes several summer stages, including stages 6 and 7 at Ülenurme Stadium due to track resurfacing
Suitable for different age groups and running distances
additional: Registration closes at 12:00 on race day. Stages 6 and 7 will take place at Ülenurme Stadium due to track resurfacing. Madsa Sports and Recreation Centre is a sports facility in Valga County supported by Tartu Sports Society Kalev, 11 km from Otepää, and is suitable for training camps and seminars. Race information includes registration, results, and upcoming dates. Participants can follow the results and view photos from previous events in the gallery.

name: Löttorpsvarvet
location: First Camp Löttorp, Löttorp, Öland, Sweden
description: Löttorpsvarvet is a family-friendly cross-country race held at First Camp Löttorp on Öland. The main distance is 6.2 km, and the course runs through woodland and meadows, with beautiful views of the Baltic Sea. Youth races of 1.4 km and 800 m are available for younger runners, and all finishers receive a medal. The event is organised by Högby IF and welcomes both recreational runners and young athletes.
course_highlights: 6.2 km of scenic cross-country running around First Camp Löttorp
Run through woodland and meadows with views of the Baltic Sea
Youth courses: 1.4 km and 800 m
additional: Register by 15 July 2026. Late registration is open until 20 July; after that, you can register when collecting your race bib on race day (from 15:00). Late registration fee: SEK 300 for Men/Women and SEK 200 for Children/Youth. Payment accepted by cash, card or Swish. Children’s/youth classes: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9, P/F11 and P/F13 (1.4 km), with separate start times; classes for ages 11 and under have no timing or prize-giving. All finishers receive a medal. Information: Jonne Svensson 070-693 87 44, Calle Nilsson 070-444 31 02. Register by 15 July 2026; late registration until 20 July; after that, at race-bib collection on race day from 15:00. Late registration fee: SEK 300 (Men/Women), SEK 200 (Children/Youth). Classes P/F11 and younger have no timing or prize-giving. Cross-country race at First Camp Löttorp, with start times for different age groups: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9 (1.4 km), P/F11 (1.4 km) and P/F13 (1.4 km).

name: Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail
description: Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail on maailman pohjoisin ultrajuoksutapahtuma, joka järjestetään Utsjoella, Lapin erämaassa. Reitti kulkee Kaldoaivin korkeimpien tunturien huipuille ja tarjoaa upeita, haastavia maisemia. Kilpailu testaa juoksijoiden kestävyyttä ja taitoja vaativassa luonnossa, mutta palkitsee kokemuksella, joka saa monet palaamaan vuosittain. Tapahtuma sisältää myös maastopyöräkilpailuja ja tarjoaa monipuolisia vaihtoehtoja eri tasoisille osallistujille.
course_highlights: Reitti kulkee Kaldoaivin korkeimpien tunturien huipuille
Upeat ja karut Lapin erämaamaisemat
Vaativa ja opettavainen polkureitti
additional: Ilmoittautuminen kahdelle päivälle antaa -30% alennuksen halvemman sarjan hinnasta. Osallistumismaksu sisältää huoltopisteiden juoma- ja energiansaannin, peseytymismahdollisuudet, varustepussin kuljetuksen maaliin, lähtönumeron, ajanoton, Kaldoaivi Ultra Trail -kevytrepun, KUT-tuotteen ja Finisher-riipuksen. Sarjan vaihdot ja siirrot ovat maksuttomia 7.7.2027 asti. Kilpailukeskukset ja lähtöpaikat ovat Nuorgamissa ja Utsjoella. Kilpailun aikataulu sisältää useita lähtöaikoja eri matkoille 23.7. ja 24.7.2027. Kilpailun osallistujakiintiöt vaihtelevat matkoittain, esimerkiksi MTB & E-MTB 57 km: 100 osallistujaa, Trailrun 168 km: 100 osallistujaa. Tapahtuma sisältää useita matkoja, joihin sisältyvät trailrun, mountain biking ja maantiepyöräily, ilman mukavuuksia reitin varrella. Osallistumiseen sisältyy kilpailunumero, aikamittauschippi, kevyt reppu ja finisher-riipus. Tapahtuma järjestetään heinäkuussa 2027, ja tarkemmat aikataulut ja ilmoittautumistiedot löytyvät verkkosivuilta.

name: Mispo maastikumaraton
location: Kurgja piirkond, Põhja-Pärnumaa vald, Pärnu maakond, Estonia
description: The Mispo Trail Marathon is a trail running event held in the Kurgja area of North Pärnumaa. Race distances are 42.195 km (marathon), 21.097 km (half marathon), 14 km and 7 km. The start is at the C.R. Jakobson Farm Museum at 11:00, and the race office opens at 9:00. All finishers receive a drink, food, access to a sauna, a diploma and a medal at the finish. The event is a tradition organized by Terviseklubi Mispo, an active sports club since 1989.
course_highlights: Trail routes in the Kurgja area
Start at the C.R. Jakobson Farm Museum
Distances: 7 km, 14 km, half marathon and marathon
additional: The race office opens at 9:00. Registration is available on race day, but the entry fee is €5 higher. All finishers receive a drink, food, access to a sauna, a diploma and a medal at the finish. The entry fee can be paid to Terviseklubi Mispo’s bank account. Trail terrain, race-day registration, medals, sauna and food.

name: Sakala metsajooks
location: Metsarada, Kurgja piirkond, Kurgja vald, Estonia
price_range: 20-35 € depending on registration date and distance
description: The Sakala Forest Run is a trail race held in the Metsarada area in Kurgja parish. The event offers several distances, including a marathon, half marathon, and shorter 7 km and 14 km races. The start is at 11:00 by the C.R. Jakobson Farm Museum. Participants are provided with a drink, food, sauna, diploma, and medal at the finish. This traditional event is organised by Terviseklubi Mispo and offers a sporting, friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: Trail course in the Metsarada area
Start by the C.R. Jakobson Farm Museum in Kurgja
Distances: 7 km, 14 km, half marathon, and marathon
additional: The race office opens at 9:00. Registration on race day is available, but the entry fee is €5 higher. All finishers receive a drink, food, sauna, diploma, and medal at the finish. The entry fee can be paid to the Terviseklubi MISPO account at SEB, IBAN: EE931010902015384003.

name: Hamra Trail Run 2026
description: Hamra Trail Run is a small, friendly trail race in stunning mountain surroundings, focused on the experience rather than a mass start. The race offers three distances—Sprint 12 km, Distance 24 km and Ultra 48 km—and starts at Pensionat Strandgården in Fjällnäs, Tänndalen. With a limited number of places (maximum 150), the organizers invite runners to enjoy views from Skenörsfjället, a sense of community and a runners’ dinner after the finish.
course_highlights: The courses mostly follow existing trails and paths through mountain terrain
Climb up and down Skenörsfjället, with views towards Malmagsvålen
Start and bib pickup at Pensionat Strandgården, Fjällnäs
additional: Mandatory equipment: your own cup (no disposable cups at the aid stations), an extra warm layer for your upper body, a wind jacket (and wind pants if needed), a buff, a first-aid kit including an elastic bandage, and a mobile phone with the safety number saved. Maximum 150 participants; registration is via MittLopp.se (links provided by the organizer). GPX files and a race guide with the safety number and practical information will be published ahead of the race. After the race, there will be a get-together and prize-giving at 15:00, followed by a runners’ dinner. Shoes with spikes or metal studs are not allowed; first-aid-trained marshals will be stationed along the course. Maximum 150 start places; registration via MittLopp.se; GPX files in the Runner’s Guide to HTR; pre-race briefing 30 minutes before the start outside Strandgården; aid stations along the course; accommodation at Strandgården or in Fjällnäs; After Run and runners’ dinner; start times: 48k 08:00, 24k 10:00, 12k 11:30.

name: KFC Südasuve Challenge - Pirita 2026
description: KFC Midsummer Challenge is a midsummer sports celebration taking place in Pirita for the third time. This community race offers beautiful views of the sea and Old Town, and a choice of three distances that participants can run or walk, or complete with a stroller or walking poles. The start and finish are conveniently located together on the shoreline, and the course follows the seaside pedestrian and cycling path without closing roads to traffic. All finishers will receive KFC gifts, and an event host and mascot will keep the spirits up.
course_highlights: Beautiful views of the sea and Old Town
Start and finish conveniently located together on the shoreline
The course follows the seaside pedestrian and cycling path without closing roads to traffic
additional: An interval-start system has been set up on the course to avoid bottlenecks. Participants can also complete the course with a stroller or walking poles. Challenges and prize draws for running enthusiasts will take place at the event and on social media. Multiple distances, a virtual participation option, a shoreline route, medals and prizes for finishers, a free concert, and themed food at KFC restaurants

name: Leigo Trail
description: Leigo Trail is a varied trail race in southern Estonia, held around the Leigo lakes. The race centre is at Leigo Tourism Farm, and the course offers a range of distance and difficulty options, making it suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. The routes follow forest trails, clay and gravel roads, and natural paths by the lake, featuring technical climbs and descents as well as beautiful views. The event brings together nature, exercise, and community, offering an enjoyable experience for the whole family.
course_highlights: An 18 km route on forest trails with steep climbs and descents; two laps of the 9 km loop
A winding 10 km clay-and-gravel route with moderate climbs; one lap
A scenic 4 km lakeside route; two laps of the 2 km loop, suitable for a first trail run
additional: The race centre is at Leigo Tourism Farm, with a race office, start and finish area, changing facilities and baggage storage, medical assistance, and catering. Free parking is available in a separate area; carpooling is recommended. Families and groups receive a 20% discount. Leigo Tourism Farm is open to visitors, and Open Farm Day takes place on the same weekend. To arrange accommodation, contact Leigo Tourism Farm. Family and group discounts are available as part of the event, and participants can choose from three distances. The course runs through natural surroundings, and registration includes various options. Parking and transport services are planned for race day.

name: Iigaste metsajooks
price_range: 4 euro (veteranid ja põhivõistlus), 8 euro kohapeal, tasuta lastejooksud ja NM18
description: The Iigaste Forest Run is part of the Rein Leppik Valgamaa Running and Nordic Walking Series, held every summer. This forest run gives participants the chance to enjoy beautiful nature and a sporting challenge on the 7.4 km main run, as well as shorter running and Nordic walking distances. The event takes place in Iigaste village and is suitable for different age groups, with medals and certificates awarded to the best finishers. Entry is affordable, and registration is conveniently available online.
course_highlights: 7.4 km main run on forest roads
3.7 km run and Nordic walking on the shorter distances
The event takes place amid the beautiful nature of Iigaste village
additional: Participation in the children’s races and the NM18 age group is free. The top three finishers in each age group receive a medal and certificate. Participants are responsible for their own health. Supporters are Eesti Kultuurkapital, Valgamaa Spordiliit, Mapco.ee and Iigaste village. The event takes place on a forest trail. Registration is through https://timesport.ee. Participants can choose from different distances, and the event is part of the Valgamaa Running and Nordic Walking Series.

name: Salomon 27K
location: Ottsjö, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Salomon 27K is a 27 km mountain-running event that is part of Fjällmaratonveckan and crosses three mountains, finishing in the scenic village of Ottsjö. The race is described as picturesque and is considered by many to be one of Sweden’s most beautiful. The course is pure mountain terrain, with magnificent views and challenging running across mountain sections.
course_highlights: 27 kilometres of mountain terrain
Crosses three mountains
Finishes in scenic surroundings in Ottsjö
additional: Food and hydration stations along the course (see provisional menu); cup-free hydration stations with kåsa drinking vessels; bus transfers to the start from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, and back after the finish; electronic chip timing; mountain safety organisation; option to transfer a race entry for a fee (250 kr); recommendation to use the Startklar insurance. Results and live updates are available; race entries can be transferred if needed; sponsors include Kia and Fjälltransfer Partners

name: Pajūrio basatlonas
description: Pajūrio Basatlonas is a unique barefoot run on the seaside sand, held in Smiltynė, Klaipėda. The event takes place during the Sea Festival and gives participants an unforgettable experience of running between the sea and the dunes. The race promotes running culture in Lithuania and encourages a healthy lifestyle. Participants can choose from several distances and enjoy the beautiful coastal scenery and gentle breeze.
course_highlights: Barefoot running on seaside sand
Start on the beach by the southern pier, Kopgalis, Smiltynė
Distances of 500 m, 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km, with a 2-hour time limit
additional: A 2-hour time limit applies to all distances. Participants must have an identity document, a race number attached, and an electronic timing chip attached to their shirt. Participants run voluntarily and assume all risks associated with taking part. Barefoot running on seaside sand, various distances (500 m, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km), online registration, regulations and rules, awards and commemorative medals.

name: Peak Performance Vertical K
description: Peak Performance Vertical K is a prestigious, fast and demanding uphill race held every year on Tuesday evening during Kia Fjällmaraton. The race starts en masse from Åre Torg and finishes at the summit of Åreskutan, with exactly 1,000 vertical metres of elevation gain. Expect maximum effort from start to finish; the course records to beat are Emmie Collinge’s 46:24 and Kilian Jornet’s 39:13. The organiser works with Peak Performance, which has developed a training programme for those who want to prepare specifically for Vertical K.
course_highlights: Mass start from Åre Torg
Finish at the summit of Åreskutan — exactly 1,000 vertical metres of elevation gain
Fast, steep uphill course; course records: Emmie Collinge 46:24, Kilian Jornet 39:13
additional: Prize money is awarded to the top three in the men’s and women’s categories. The organiser has developed a six-week training programme in the Peak Performance Strava Club. A course image/map is published (map_verticalk.png on the website). According to sources, it is uniquely Sweden’s only vertical kilometre; it is part of Fjällmaratonveckan (Kia Fjällmaratonveckan) and AXA Fjällmaratonveckan, according to blog posts. The course is said to be approximately 5 km long according to the blog, and a training link is available via the Peak Performance Strava Club.

name: 10. ETAPP
description: TV 10 Olympic Start is a competition series organized by the Estonian Athletics Association for schoolchildren and young athletes. Competitions are held in different age groups and include a variety of track and field events. The 10th stage takes place on 29 July 2026 at Tamme Stadium in Tartu, giving young people the opportunity to test their skills and gain experience. The series aims to support young people’s athletic development and provide a fun and motivating competitive environment.
course_highlights: Competitions take place at Tamme Stadium in Tartu
A variety of track and field events for different age groups
Open to schoolchildren and young athletes
additional: Registration takes place half an hour before the competitions begin. The top three in each event and age group are awarded medals, and the best performances receive special prizes. The competition is part of the TV 10 Olympic Start series and supports the development and competitiveness of young athletes.

name: Fjällmaraton 100k
description: Fjällmaraton 100K is a long, classic mountain run that starts at dawn in Fångåmon and is part of Kia Fjällmaraton Årefjällen. The first part of the course follows a beautiful, winding and runnable trail towards Vålådalen via Nulltjärn, before joining the classic Fjällmaraton route over the imposing Ottfjället. Runners continue over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste on the way back to the finish in Ottsjö. The race is demanding and self-supported: participants must manage their own hydration and nutrition between the official aid stations.
course_highlights: Beautiful, winding and runnable trail towards Vålådalen via Nulltjärn
Classic climb over the imposing Ottfjället
Sections over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste through mountain terrain
additional: All participants must be self-supported during the race: refill at official aid stations or use natural water sources; support outside the official stations is not permitted. Official sports drink: U Sport by Umara (lemon, mixed at 90 g/litre), with gluten-free U-bars available at the stations. Key stations and approximate distances: Vålådalen 22 km, Nordbottnen 38 km, Ottsjö (drop bag) 51.5 km, Tobaksdalen 65 km, Edsåsdalen 77.5 km, Skavhugget 82.5 km, Ytterstvallen 92.5 km, Finish 100 km. Post-race food is served by Fävikens Lanthandel. The organisers run Ottsjö 8K in the evening to create a great atmosphere at the finish. Drop bags are available in Ottsjö (51.5 km); U Sport by Umara sports drink and gluten-free U-bars are mentioned in the general information; start time 05:00; approximately 3,300 metres of elevation gain; transfer and travel options via Kia Fjälltransfer during Fjällmaraton Week.

name: Vormsi maraton
location: Sviby Harbour, Vormsi Island, Vormsi Parish, Lääne County, Estonia
description: Vormsi Marathons VIII is a two-day running event on Vormsi Island, taking place on July 31 and August 1 near Sviby Harbour. Participants can choose the marathon or half-marathon distance on either day, with the routes running mainly on paved roads on Vormsi Island. The routes are marked, and timing is recorded using electronic SI sticks. After the run, participants can enjoy a social get-together, a sauna and hot soup at the finish. The event is small and friendly, suited to both experienced runners and recreational runners.
course_highlights: The marathon route runs along Vormsi Island’s main paved roads
The half-marathon route passes through the villages of Hullo, Rälby, Diby and Norrby
The route follows hard-surfaced public roads, with turns marked
additional: The start and finish are on the square in front of the kiosk near Sviby Harbour. There is no course support; supplies can be replenished at the Hullo shop. The marathon is timed at one intermediate checkpoint and at the finish; the half-marathon is timed only at the finish. Every finisher receives a commemorative medal. After the run, participants can enjoy a social get-together and use the sauna. On Saturday, the finish closes at 16:45; on Friday, it stays open as long as needed. A purchased entry is valid for one or both days. It is not possible to complete both distances on the same day. Two-day run; no course support; camping or campground accommodation available; transport from Rohuküla.

name: 28. Holstre-Paistu maanteejooks Hanno Priksi mälestuseks
description: Holstre-Paistu Road Race is the fourth stage of Viljandi Municipality’s running series and takes place in Paistu. The race is intended for runners of all abilities and offers young people and adults alike the opportunity to take part. Participation in the series motivates runners to complete all four stages, and active participants are rewarded. The course runs through the scenic Viljandi County, offering an enjoyable running experience.
course_highlights: Road race in the Paistu area
Participation opportunities in different age groups
Participants are motivated by awards in the running series

name: Mapri Ehitus x Öövägilane
location: Lähte terviserad, Lähte, Tartu County, Estonia

price_tiers.distance: Mapri Ehitus x Öövägilane Lähte 5 km

description: Mapri Ehitus x Öövägilane is an obstacle race held on the Lähte health trails. It is a varied and challenging run where participants climb, crawl, lift and drag themselves through mud, water, sand and hills. The event is suitable for both beginners and experienced obstacle racers, offering an exciting and fun experience. The series aims to offer a multi-day competition, with each stage having its own character and an emphasis on both fun and physical challenge.
course_highlights: 5 km course on the Lähte health trails
A variety of obstacles: climbing, crawling, lifting and dragging
Mud, water, sand and hills along the course
additional: A 15% discount applies when registering for at least three Vägilase jooks events at once. Payment via Stebby is possible. Discounts for young people under 20 and seniors aged 60 and over are applied automatically based on year of birth. Group discount of 20% for registering at least 4 people for the same event. The competition takes place over several days; each stage has its own character, with an emphasis on both fun and physical challenge. Participants take part at their own risk. Registration is open until 1 August. The entry fee includes a race number, medal, drink and snacks.

name: Mapri Ehitus x Vägilase jooks Lähte
location: Lähte terviseradad ja jõulinnakus, Lähte, Estonia
description: Mapri Ehitus x Vägilase Run Lähte is an obstacle race held on the Lähte health trails and at the strength-training park. The courses are 4 km and 8 km long and offer participants a serious challenge, with a variety of obstacles testing both strength and agility. Vägilase Run is Estonia’s most versatile obstacle-race series event, suitable for both beginners and experienced obstacle racers. The event is part of a series focused on terrain, obstacles and an adventurous experience.
course_highlights: 4 km and 8 km obstacle courses on the Lähte health trails and at the strength-training park
A variety of obstacles testing strength and agility
Mud, water, sand and hills along the course
additional: Children’s runs for participants up to 14 years old are free (when registered online before the event); on-site registration costs €3. All finishers in the children’s runs receive a medal and a treat. Participants are responsible for their own health; minors may participate with parental permission. There is no overall series ranking, but participants who take part in at least three stages receive a gift at the end of the season. Registering for at least three events at once gives a 15% discount. Vägilase Run shirts are available to purchase at a discounted price in December. Participants can register online, and the event has different categories and discounts. The course follows existing trails and roads, and the obstacles are built to be challenging and safe. Participation is at one’s own risk, and the event is open to all age groups.

name: Ottsjö 12k
description: Ottsjö 12K is a 12 km mountain race with around 300 metres of elevation gain, offering a beautiful but demanding course through mountain terrain. It is an option for those who want to experience the mountain landscape without taking on the full distance or Salomon 27K. The route starts in Ottsjö and climbs towards Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas shelter, then continues along the plateau trail past Platåkåtan. It finishes by descending through the village and following Lake Ottsjön to the finish in the meadows in Ottsjö. The organiser offers a family option (children aged 10–13 run with an adult for SEK 200), and young people aged 14–18 pay half the entry fee.
course_highlights: Mountain terrain with around 300 metres of elevation gain
Climb towards Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas shelter, then follow the plateau trail past Platåkåtan
Descend through the village and follow Lake Ottsjön to the finish in the meadows in Ottsjö
additional: Start times are listed as 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30. Children aged 10–13 can run with an adult for SEK 200; otherwise, the minimum age is 14. Young people aged 14–18 pay half the entry fee. Electronic chip timing; food and drink stations featuring local food; a traditional wooden cup is used at cup-free stations. Bus transfers to the start are available from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, with transfers back after the finish. 12 km, ~300 m elevation gain; start in Ottsjö; children’s option for ages 10–13 costs SEK 200 with an adult; minimum age 14; accompanying runners must stay in contact with minors; ages 14–18 pay half price; start times: 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30.

name: Bruksleden Terrängmaraton
description: Welcome to Bruksleden Terrängmaraton, a friendly trail race along the beautiful Bruksleden on Saturday, 1 August 2026. The race offers two distances: 42 km (Helan) and 21 km (Halvan), and is suitable for both experienced trail runners and curious recreational runners. The courses pass through forests, along winding trails and by lakes, with varied and sometimes technically demanding terrain. The number of starting places is limited to preserve the welcoming atmosphere, and there are staffed checkpoints along the course. After finishing, showers and a light meal are available.
course_highlights: Running on Bruksleden’s winding forest trails
Sections passing lakes and beautiful forest scenery
Varied, sometimes technical terrain with steep climbs and descents
additional: Two distances: 42 km (Helan) and 21 km (Halvan). Limited number of starting places: 200. The deadline for standard registration is 17 July 2026; late registration is available through 30 July 2026 for a 50% surcharge. There are staffed checkpoints along the course for refills. Course profiles and routes (21 km and 42 km), as well as maps, are published on the organiser’s pages. The organiser reserves the right to make changes to the course. Gathering/start information is listed as 10:00; after finishing, showers and a light meal are available. The number of starting places for Helan and Halvan is limited, to approximately 200 participants. The finish area at Fageråsen includes showers and catering.

name: Vääna-Jõesuu jooks
location: Vääna-Jõesuu Kooli staadion, Vääna-Jõesuu, Harku vald, Harju maakond, Estonia
description: The Vääna-Jõesuu Run is part of the Harku Municipality running series and takes place on August 2, 2026, at the Vääna-Jõesuu School stadium. The event offers several distances, from children’s races to the 5 km main race, which follows the streets of Vääna-Jõesuu and a forest road in a counterclockwise direction. The series aims to motivate people to take part in sports and promote the joy of movement and an active lifestyle. The event is organized by local running and triathlon clubs in cooperation with the municipality and village associations.
course_highlights: 5 km route along the streets of Vääna-Jõesuu and a forest road
The route runs counterclockwise
Children’s races on the stadium track (220 m and 660 m)
additional: The event center opens at 11:00, the main race starts at 12:00, the awards ceremony is at 13:00, and the children’s races start at 13:30. On-site registration and changes to registration are available until 15 minutes before the start. Awards are given to the top three men and women in each age group and the top three families in the family competition. The family competition is for mothers, fathers, and children, who earn points based on their age-group placements. More information about registration, event sponsors, and raffle prizes is available on the website. Participants are responsible for their own health, and the event is open to all age groups.

name: ÜLEMISTE Ööjooks - Tallinn 2026
description: ÜLEMISTE Night Run - Tallinn 2026 is a running and walking event taking place in the Ülemiste district of Tallinn. The event offers an opportunity to get active and support well-being and health. It is part of a wider initiative to promote recreational physical activity in Estonia, organised by the Centre of Competence for Recreational Physical Activity. Participants can enjoy being active in an urban environment and support their mental and physical health.
course_highlights: Running and walking in the Ülemiste district of Tallinn
A great opportunity to get active and support your health
Organised by the Centre of Competence for Recreational Physical Activity
additional: Participation involves running and walking; registration is open

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 20. Tapa linnajooks
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series is a traditional running and walking series offering a variety of opportunities for different age groups and ability levels. Its events take place in different locations across Lääne-Virumaa, giving runners the chance to experience both urban and trail running. The 20th Tapa City Run takes place on 8 August 2026 at Tapa Gymnasium and is part of the series’ long-standing tradition of bringing together recreational athletes and running enthusiasts. The series aims to motivate people to stay active and provide enjoyable running experiences.
course_highlights: A varied route in an urban setting
Suitable for different age groups and ability levels
Part of a long-running series in Lääne-Virumaa
additional: The series offers different distances and age groups, including youth and children’s races. Events take place in different locations across Lääne-Virumaa, with both urban and trail runs. Registration is usually via online forms, but no direct registration link for the 20th Tapa City Run was found. The series contacts are Vahur Leemets and Ainar Sepnik. The event takes place at Tapa Gymnasium and offers online registration. Participants can choose from different distances, and awards are presented at every event.

name: Paldiski liigub
description: Paldiski Moves is the third stage of the Western Harju Movement Series and takes place at Paldiski Sports Centre. The course passes Paldiski’s main attractions, streets and pedestrian and cycling paths, offering participants beautiful natural views and a historic atmosphere. Free children’s races are held for younger family members, emphasising the joy of movement and lifelong awareness of physical activity. The event takes place as part of Paldiski City Day, where the series’ top finishers are awarded prizes, and the evening ends with a concert.
course_highlights: The course passes Paldiski’s main attractions
Runs along streets and pedestrian and cycling paths
Beautiful natural views and a historic atmosphere
additional: Chip timing is used, except for the untimed distance. The children’s races are free and intended for children aged 0–12. There are no placements; every finisher receives a diploma. The event is held in cooperation with Paldiski City Day, which offers activities for the whole family, and the series’ top three finishers are awarded prizes on the main stage. The evening ends with a concert. The children’s races are free, the course passes attractions, and chip timing is used (except for the untimed distance).

name: Kia Fjällmaraton 45 km
description: Kia Fjällmaraton 45K is a demanding mountain marathon across classic mountain terrain, held during Fjällmaraton Week in the Åre area. The race dates back to 2005, and for 2026 the course is planned to cross Ottfjället along the event’s signature trail. The race welcomes both experienced mountain runners and curious beginners looking for an unusual and scenic challenge. To earn the well-known wooden medal, you must finish within the “medal time” (the winner’s time + 30%); all participants must be self-sufficient on the course.
course_highlights: The course crosses Ottfjället over classic mountain terrain
Food and hydration stations at Edsåsdalen (12 km, 25 km), Tobaksdalen (35.5 km), and Hållvallen (40 km)
Finish in Ottsjö, with a shared post-race lunch for all finishers
additional: Participants must be self-sufficient on the course; the official hydration product at the stations is Umara (2:1 lemon, 120 g/l). Water and toilets are available at the start in Trillevallen. Support along the course is not permitted except at the official stations. In addition to drinks, the stations offer bars, bananas, buns, and, at later stations, hot dogs, coffee, and broth. The race is approximately 45 km long with around 1,200 metres of elevation gain (according to a race report). Participants are self-sufficient between aid stations; official food and hydration are available at Edsåsdalen, Tobaksdalen, and Hållvallen. Kia offers Fjälltransfer, with free transfers between the finish and the parking area, as well as a bus between the finish and Undersåker/Åre. Accommodation in Åre near Kia Fjällmaraton includes, among other options, Hotel Åre Fjällsätra.

name: Stora Stöten Run
description: Stora Stöten Run is a trail race in the heart of the Falun Mine World Heritage Site, offering a historic and varied running experience. The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses, following old routes known as Vattnets Väg till Gruvan (The Water’s Way to the Mine). The race has three distances (21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km) and welcomes both competitive runners and recreational participants, with the option to run timed or untimed. The event is organised by the orienteering club OK Kåre, which welcomes participants to the start and finish at Falun Mine.
course_highlights: Three courses: 21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km, starting and finishing at Falun Mine
The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses along Vattnets Väg
Varied terrain: gravel, grass, trail tracks, nature paths and short paved sections; an initial climb and clearly marked downhill sections
additional: Start and finish at Falun Mine; warm-up begins at 12:10 on Falu Rödfärg’s paved area (approximately 7 minutes), led by Friskis & Svettis; all courses start at the same time, and runners are divided into two optional groups based on target pace (group 1: women ≤6 min/km, men ≤5 min/km). Runners can choose to run with or without timing; prizes go to the first three finishers on each course, with raffle prizes for other participants; teams can be registered (teams of 3), and registrations can be transferred free of charge through the registration system. The race information mentions aid stations/water stops, parking, race office, showers/changing facilities and course markings. All three courses start and finish at Falun Mine; results from previous years are available.

name: Ölands Marathon
description: Öland Marathon is an open marathon starting and finishing in the square in Löttorp. The course is very flat and easy to run, entirely paved, and offers views of Blå Jungfrun. The race consists of an inner loop of 2.1 km and an outer loop of 11.2 km, repeated three times until the distance of 42.195 km is reached. The race is organised by Högby IF and is aimed at recreational runners and masters categories in the stated divisions.
course_highlights: Very flat, easy-to-run marathon course
100% paved, officially measured by federation course measurer Carl‑Gustaf Nilsson
Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; a 2.1 km inner loop plus an 11.2 km outer loop repeated 3 times, with views of Blå Jungfrun
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 12:00. There are three aid stations per lap (approx. 13.3 km), serving sports drink (Umara), Coca-Cola and water; personal energy supplies must be handed in no later than one hour before the start. All finishers receive a medal/fossil made of Öland limestone; ÖM medals go to the top two in each category. The women’s and men’s winners receive dinner for two at Kalk in Löttorp. Accommodation is available in four-bed cabins at Högby IP. Aid stations: three per lap. The course consists of a 2.1 km section in Löttorp followed by an 11.2 km section: Löttorp - Alvedsjö - Kalmarsund - Gudesjö - Löttorp, repeated three times for a total of 42.195 km. Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; accommodation information is available via links on the organiser’s website.

name: Svartåloppet
description: Svartåloppet is a recurring running event held on the second Saturday in August, bringing together runners over several distances. The event offers 14 km and 5.5 km on hilly forest roads and trails, as well as a flat 2.5 km route on roads. The start and finish are at Svartå Folketshus, and timing is provided by Racetimer, delivering modern and reliable results. The event welcomes both recreational and competitive runners and highlights the local landscape and trail network.
course_highlights: 14 km and 5.5 km: hilly forest course on forest roads and trails
2.5 km: flatter route on roads
Start and finish at Svartå Folketshus
additional: Timing for Svartåloppet is provided by Racetimer, and results from previous years are published via Racetimer. The event is held annually on the second Saturday in August. The website contact is listed as Svartå Utvecklingsgrupp, telephone number 076 3073096. Three distances; children's race includes a medal and bag of sweets; on-site registration is available at the stated times (09:00–10:30), according to the event information.

name: Arctic Circle Race
price_range: 2480 SEK inklusive helikoptertransfer; 1490 SEK utan helikoptertransfer
description: Arctic Circle Race is a trail race in the heart of the mountains, where participants are flown by helicopter to the start at Guijaure and run approximately 18 km along the Arctic Circle back to civilisation. The race combines adventure and competition and offers the choice of a helicopter transfer or hiking to the start independently. The course is technical and varied, with narrow trails, rocky slabs and a short but steep climb called “the Wall”. Arctic Circle Race 2026 takes place on Saturday, 8 August, and prices are listed separately for participants with and without a helicopter transfer.
course_highlights: Helicopter drop-off at the start at Guijaure, followed by a run along the Arctic Circle (approx. 18 km).
Varied, rocky and often narrow mountain terrain, with the steep climb known as “the Wall” at ~8 km and the final ~4 km running sharply downhill.
Two water stations (approx. 6 km and 12 km); start at 690 m above sea level, highest point at 805 m above sea level, finish at 480 m above sea level.
additional: Optional helicopter transfer (with or without helicopter). Share a helicopter by registering several participants at the same time — sequential bib numbers and the same start time. Check-in, parking and helicopter pick-up at Camp Polcirkeln, Polcirkeln 3, 93894 Arjeplog. Timing is done using a chip integrated into the bib. First aid and staff are available at the water stations, and a helicopter is on standby for serious incidents. Includes a helicopter to the start and the option of a round trip between Arjeplog and Camp Polcirkeln for 500 SEK, according to the information on the English-language page.

name: Nätra Fjällskogslopp
location: Hinnsjöstugan, Nätra fjällskog, Örnsköldsviks kommun, Sweden
description: Nätra Fjällskogslopp is organised by Nätra GIF ungdom and is a scenic trail race held at Hinnsjöstugan in Nätra fjällskog. The first race took place in 2021, and the event offers challenging but enjoyable courses through forests, over boardwalks across wetlands and along winding trails with beautiful views. There are four distances (22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km for children), and the organisers encourage both competitive runners and recreational runners to choose their place in the field according to their ability. The start and finish are at Hinnsjöstugan, with clear markings and services for participants.
course_highlights: Trails, forest roads and boardwalks across wetlands—varied trail running
Views from Västerselsbodarna and Västanåhöjden (with a chance to glimpse Ulvön)
Long downhill stretches towards the finish, with views over Hinnsjön
additional: Organiser: Nätra GIF ungdom. Start location: Startstugan Hinnsjön (address: Hinnsjön 100, Sidensjö). Parking is signposted along the road near Hinnsjöstugan, a short walk from the start. Race bibs must be collected by 09:00 at the latest for the 22 km, 15 km and 9 km races. A bag drop is available at Hinnsjöstugan. Recommended equipment: mobile phone, fluids/energy and a course map. Start times: 22 km 09:30, 15 km 09:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. Course markings use different colours (22/15 km: blue/yellow; 9 km: red/yellow; 2 km: yellow). Participants are asked to stay on the marked trails, use the boardwalks and take their rubbish to the finish. The route passes through two nature reserves (Västanåhöjden and Stakamyras), which have special regulations. Distances are 22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km (children). Start times according to the information: 22 km 9:30, 15 km 9:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. The event runs as a full-day activity from 10:30 to 16:00 and is stated to be fully booked.

name: Ångaloppet Trail
description: Ångaloppet is a welcoming swimrun event at Ånga gård, with the aim of making “swimrun for everyone.” The 2026 races take place on 8 August and include several distances and events for different levels, including 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The courses feature varied landscapes with forest trails, gravel roads and hilly, technical terrain; the swimrun races also include several swim sections in both lake and sea. The organisers emphasise a welcoming atmosphere for participants of all ages and experience levels.
course_highlights: Varied forest, trails and gravel roads
Hilly, technical terrain suited to trail running
Located between Lake Ången and the Baltic Sea—combining running and swimming (for the swimrun distances)
additional: In 2026, the event comprises five races on the same day (8 August): 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The 22 km race is a loop course (11 km per lap), with approximately 20 swim sections in total (the longest about 190 m and the shortest about 30 m), six aid stations along the course and a cutoff of 2.5 hours at the lap point. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK—email info@angaloppet.se. The courses are marked, and start group 1 (the earliest start) is listed at 10:00. Ångaloppet Trail is a new distance in the 2026 programme. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK. More information about equipment, safety, accommodation and parking is available on the event pages.

name: Häv och Gräv Vikbovändan 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: vuxen 470 kr (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar loppet 520 kr)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: duoklass: 940 kr per par (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar duolopp 1040 kr)

description: Häv & Gräv Vikbovändan is a summer event on Vikbolandet in Östergötland where participants can choose to run or cycle. The main course is approximately 45 km long and runs mostly on paved roads and gravel (about 50/50), with several aid stations and samples from local farms along the way. There are categories for runners, cyclists, duos and children, and the event has a clear focus on local producers and an authentic farm setting. Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup (folding cup), which they must bring during the event to avoid disposable cups.
course_highlights: Main course approximately 45 km, about 50/50 gravel and asphalt
Aid stations at several local farms, with delicacies and opportunities to visit the farms
Opportunities to meet and sample products at farms with animals (ostriches, alpacas and yaks)
additional: The number of participants in the main event is limited (300). Online registration is open until 4 August; late registration is available from 09:00 in the start area until 30 minutes before each start (if places are available). Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup, which must be used during the event. The children's race (approximately 700 m or 1,400 m) requires no advance registration and is free for participants thanks to sponsorship from ICA (children receive a medal and ice cream). Toilets and showers are available at APPTEK's premises (open approximately 09:30–18:30). The running category is timed, with prizes for the top three women and men; the cycling and duo categories have special rules (helmets are compulsory, e-bikes are not allowed, and duo partners may swap as often as they like but must stay within 100 m of each other). There is a group warm-up before the start. Aid stations offer water and sports drinks; pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup; everyone receives a medal; the event is not sanctioned by the Swedish Athletics Association; helmets are compulsory for cycling; the start and finish are in a floodlit trail setting; medical staff are on site; image rights rules apply. Register at vikbovandan.se/472-2/ or via the registration page on the main website.

name: Kivijärviloppet
description: Kivijärviloppet is a traditional cross-country race organized by Kivijärvi IF since 1970. The event is held in the village of Kivijärvi in the Torne Valley and has grown to more than 200 participants. The main event is the 12 km open class for both women and men, and the race is known for its generous prize table thanks to its sponsors. Many well-known skiers and runners have taken part over the years, giving the race strong local and national standing.
course_highlights: Cross-country race with courses marked in different colors: 0.5 km and 1.5 km (yellow), 5 km (white), 7.5 km (blue), 12 km (red)
The race takes place in the beautiful Torne Valley in eastern Norrbotten
The courses have remained unchanged since the race began in 1970, except during the COVID pandemic
additional: Course routes are marked in different colors for each distance: 0.5 km and 1.5 km (yellow), 5 km (white), 7.5 km (blue), 12 km (red). The event offers a generous prize table for children, adults, and recreational runners, thanks to generous sponsors. The race offers several categories, including a 12 km open class, and is known for its prize money and for bringing together participants of different ability levels. The course runs mainly along natural forest trails.

name: Storå 6 timmars och 3 timmars
location: Guldsmedshyttan, Lindesberg Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden

name: VI Ilgų nuotolių bėgiko Piotro Silkino jubiliejinis 85-mečio bėgimas
location: Kretingos Vasaros estrada, Maironio g. 15, Kretinga, Lithuania
description: The 85th-birthday run of long-distance runner Piotr Silkin is a traditional race held at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre. The competition follows a lap format, with marathon participants completing one 2.2 km lap and twelve 3.3 km laps. The event celebrates longtime runner Piotr Silkin and attracts running enthusiasts from various places. Participants can enjoy both athletic competition and a welcoming community atmosphere.
course_highlights: The marathon course consists of 1 lap of 2.2 km and 12 laps of 3.3 km each
The competition takes place at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre
The lap format lets spectators follow the race and support the participants
additional: Various distances and age groups will be offered at the event; results will be published, and registration is online.

name: Kohila pikamaajooksude sari 2026 VI etapp 1000m
location: Kohila Spordikeskuse staadion, Kohila, Kohila vald, Estonia
description: Kohila Long-Distance Running Series 2026, Stage VI (1000 m), takes place at the Kohila Sports Centre stadium and is open to all running enthusiasts. The series features various distances and age groups, with participants earning points and winners determined by age group. The entry fee is €8, or €5 for young people and pensioners. Registration is primarily online in advance; on-site registration is available until 18:30. Series winners are awarded after the final race. To qualify for an award, participants must take part in at least four stages.
course_highlights: 400 m tartan running track at Kohila Stadium
Races over various distances, from 400 m to 5000 m
Age groups from young people to Veterans III (60+)
additional: Advance registration closes at 16:30 on race day. Late registrants are placed in the later heats, regardless of their expected time. On-site registration closes at 18:30. The top 10 in each race earn points; the total is calculated from each participant’s six best race results. Series winners are awarded after the final race. The entry fee is payable in cash on site. Advance registration is available at www.kohilaseeriajooksud.ee. Races take place at Kohila Stadium. Age categories and a points system are in place.

name: Filter Temposari (5. etapp)
description: Filter Temposari is Estonia’s oldest and most prestigious time-trial series, offering participants the chance to test themselves in cycling, running, or roller skating. The stages take place at various locations in Tallinn and the surrounding area, featuring individual time trials. The races are short and intense, suitable for both recreational and advanced athletes. The series also includes the Kullapada prize programme, which rewards consistent participation in every stage over the same distance.
course_highlights: Fast individual time-trial courses around Tallinn
Short 3–5 km runs and 7–17 km cycling courses
A new city sprint in the heart of Tallinn, featuring a 1.3 km course with a climb to Toompea
additional: Timing is accurate to a tenth of a second. Free warm-up trainers are available at the event centre. Hot Group: the final 10 minutes of each stage are reserved for the top cyclists. The courses are not closed to cars; competitors must obey traffic laws and keep to the right-hand side of the road. “I don’t have a time-trial bike” is no excuse—a standard road bike may be used. The event takes place at several different locations in Tallinn and includes time trials, sprint races, and special events such as the city sprint and series prizes.

name: 14. ETAPP / Järve terviserada
description: STAGE 14 / Järve health trail is a 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi, held on a health trail with varied terrain and different surface types. Teams consist of 10 members, with equal numbers of women and men, who take turns running the different stages. The start and finish are at Viljandi City Stadium, and organizers’ buses transport runners to the stages. The race is part of the tradition of the Great Run Around Lake Viljandi and offers a sporting experience for schools, companies, and sports clubs alike.
course_highlights: 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi on a health trail
Varied terrain and trails with different surfaces
Stages range in length from 500 m to 1,950 m
additional: Teams consist of 10 members (5 women and 5 men). Women run the odd-numbered stages and men run the even-numbered stages. Teams from institutions and companies may, as an exception, use a female runner on men’s stages. The entry fee is €50 for institutions, companies, and sports clubs; school teams pay no entry fee. Teams can register by email until 12 April, and runners must be registered by name at the stadium on 14 April. The awards ceremony takes place at 13:30 at the stadium. The three leading teams receive trophies and diplomas, and every participant receives a medal. Depending on trail conditions, the course may be changed to avoid muddy or snowy sections. A 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi, varied terrain, registration by email, start and finish at Viljandi City Stadium.

name: 31. Joosu Järvejooksu sarja 5. etapp
location: Viljandi Lake Health and Ski Trail, Viljandi, Estonia
description: The 5th stage of the Joosu Lake Run series is a running race organized by the Joosu sports club. It takes place on the health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi. The race gives participants the opportunity to enjoy beautiful lake views and varied terrain. It is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to take part in a friendly and supportive environment.
course_highlights: Health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi
Beautiful lake views along the route
Varied terrain suitable for runners

name: Trail- & Ultravasan (Vasaloppet)
description: Vasaloppet organises a summer week of running and mountain biking, including races such as Ultravasan and Trailvasan. The events take place in mid-August and attract tens of thousands of registered participants each year. Registration and practical information are available at vasaloppet.se. The event is organised by Vasaloppet, a non-profit organisation owned by IFK Mora and Sälens IF.
course_highlights: Part of Vasaloppet’s summer week of running and mountain biking
Includes the Ultravasan 90 and Trailvasan (10/30) distances in mid-August
Organised by Vasaloppet (owned by IFK Mora and Sälens IF)
additional: Registration is through Vasaloppet’s registration pages at vasaloppet.se; registering early means a lower price. For company registrations and group bookings, contact foretag@vasaloppet.se. Vasaloppet customer service can be reached by phone at 0250-392 00, and general enquiries at info@vasaloppet.se. Ultravasan 90 is part of Vasaloppstrippeln 90; bib and chip collection is in Mora/Sälen; baggage transport to Mora and Evertsberg; medals and an award ceremony are promised. Trailvasan 10 has a maximum of 1,000 participants, an age limit of 11+, and a start opportunity until 18:15; there are two water/aid stations along the course.

name: BAMM
location: Björkliden, Kiruna Municipality, Norrbotten County, Sweden
description: BAMM (Björkliden Arctic Mountain Marathon) is a mountain orienteering competition in the Björkliden/Riksgränsen area, where participants compete in pairs (men’s, women’s or mixed teams). The competition takes place across large areas of unmarked mountain terrain and is geared towards adventure and orienteering in a mountain environment. The event is presented in collaboration with its main partner, OMM, and the competition website includes practical information about travel, accommodation and the programme. The event is aimed at orienteers seeking a challenging competition experience in an Arctic mountain setting.
course_highlights: Mountain orienteering across large areas of unmarked mountain terrain
Competition format: pairs (men’s, women’s or mixed teams)
Held in the Björkliden/Riksgränsen mountain region near the Norwegian border
additional: Practical travel information is available on the website: transfers can be booked from Kiruna Airport to Hotell Riksgränsen (with connections to SAS/Norwegian flights), as well as return transfers. Travel by train via SJ to Riksgränsen takes approximately 18 hours from Stockholm, and Riksgränsen railway station is about 100 metres from Hotell Riksgränsen. The website also includes the programme and participant list for BAMM 2026, as well as accommodation and Arctic Skibus information. Two-day mountain orienteering in the Björkliden area; mandatory personal and team equipment; approximately 230 starting teams per edition; BAMM 30 includes transport of tent and sleeping-bag equipment to the overnight camp; registration via ReadySetGo.

name: Trail- & Ultravasan
location: Sälen and Mora, Dalarna County, Sweden
description: Ultravasan 90 is a challenging ultramarathon that follows the classic Vasaloppet Trail from Sälen to Mora. The race starts early in the morning in Berga by and offers a scenic, historic running experience through pine forests, winding waterways and summer pasture farms. Participants can enjoy a well-organised race with several aid stations and the option to transport change-of-clothes bags to different checkpoints. Ultravasan 90 is part of Vasaloppstrippeln and attracts runners from around the world who want to test their endurance on a spectacular course.
course_highlights: Start in Berga by, Sälen, with sunrise over the marshes at Smågan
7 official checkpoints with drinks and energy, including Evertsberg, where drop bags can be collected
Scenic pine forests, winding waterways and summer pasture farms along the entire course
additional: Race numbers and timing chips can be collected in Sälen or Mora the day before, or at the start area. The start corrals open at 04:30. Change-of-clothes bags can be dropped off in Sälen for transport to Mora or Evertsberg. Toilets and medical care are available at all checkpoints and in the start and finish areas. Massage is offered in Evertsberg and Hökberg. Official checkpoints with drinks and energy are located at Smågan, Mångsbodarna, Risberg, Evertsberg, Oxberg, Hökberg and Eldris. The event is part of Vasaloppstrippeln. Trail ultramarathon, checkpoints, gear transport, medals, start in Sälen, finish in Mora, Swedish Championship status 2026, maximum 2500 participants

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 27. Viru-Nigula Rahvajooks
location: Viru-Nigula jooksurada ja kaugushüppekast, Viru-Nigula, Lääne-Virumaa, Estonia
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 offers a varied series of running and walking events, bringing together recreational athletes and enthusiasts from spring to autumn. The 27th Viru-Nigula Fun Run takes place on the Viru-Nigula running track and long-jump runway. It is part of a long-standing series that encourages participation across different age groups and distances. The series aims to promote healthy lifestyles and give participants the chance to test their abilities. The events are well organized, with chip timing, ensuring participants an enjoyable and motivating running experience.
course_highlights: A variety of distances, from 100 m to 10 km
Running courses on the Viru-Nigula running track and long-jump runway
A traditional event in the running series, with the running direction changing
additional: Timing is provided by a chip attached to the back of the bib and covered with foam board. Bibs must be fastened to the abdomen or chest, not the back.
